# idiotproof commands

<!-- Generated by `idiotproof agent export` (or `idiotproof --export-commands`). Do not hand-edit. -->

232 operations, each also an MCP tool (`noun_verb`). Every one runs inside the IdiotProof Hub
(`idiotproof hub start`), so all data and every transaction goes through it. Global flags: `--json`, `--user <guid>`,
`--confirm <code>`, `--hub <url>`, `--no-color`, `-h`. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 usage, 3 blocked by a gate,
4 confirmation required. Times are US Eastern.

| Command | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`account activities`](#account-activities) | Read | Account activity log: fills, dividends, fees, deposits, interest, option expirations/assignments (newest first, ET). |
| [`account buying-power`](#account-buying-power) | Read | Buying power by kind (overall, Reg T, day-trading, non-marginable, options), cash and margin multiplier. |
| [`account calendar`](#account-calendar) | Read | Trading days with premarket, regular and after-hours times (ET); early closes and holidays called out. |
| [`account clock`](#account-clock) | Read | Is the market open now, and when it next opens and closes (ET), from Alpaca's clock. |
| [`account config`](#account-config) | Read | Alpaca account settings side by side: DTBP/PDT checks, shorting, fractional, margin cap, options level, trade suspension. |
| [`account config set`](#account-config-set) | Write | Change one Alpaca account setting (Live needs a confirmation code). |
| [`account history`](#account-history) | Read | Equity over time as a Braille line chart, with the true P&L (deposits excluded) for 1D to all-time windows. |
| [`account pdt`](#account-pdt) | Read | Pattern-day-trader standing: day trades in the last 5 business days, PDT flag, equity vs the $25k floor, trades left. |
| [`account summary`](#account-summary) | Read | Equity, cash, buying power and today's true P&L (deposits excluded) for your Alpaca paper and live accounts. |
| [`agent catalog`](#agent-catalog) | Read | List every operation with its parameters, risk and input schema. |
| [`assets bonds`](#assets-bonds) | Read | Alpaca fixed income assets: US Treasuries or US corporate bonds with coupon, maturity, last close and yield. |
| [`assets list`](#assets-list) | Read | Alpaca's tradable universe (/v2/assets) filtered by class, exchange, status and attributes, with totals. |
| [`assets show`](#assets-show) | Read | One Alpaca asset: tradable, shortable, easy-to-borrow, marginable, fractionable and margin requirements. |
| [`audit list`](#audit-list) | Read | The audit trail, newest first: signals, entries/exits, rejections, risk blocks, system events (ET). |
| [`audit search`](#audit-search) | Read | Find audit rows whose message or payload contains text: a symbol, order id, strategy title. |
| [`audit tail`](#audit-tail) | Read | The latest audit rows, oldest first; --follow watches for new ones for a bounded time (--seconds, --max). |
| [`backtest conditions`](#backtest-conditions) | Read | A backtest day's per-candle condition table: each entry condition's truth per bar, fires, entries and time in position. |
| [`backtest run`](#backtest-run) | Read | Backtest a saved strategy or a script over a range of ET days with StrategyBacktester: triggers, trades and P&L per day (saved for backtest conditions). |
| [`corporate-actions list`](#corporate-actions-list) | Read | Splits, dividends, mergers, spinoffs and name changes from Alpaca (Market Data or Trading API announcements) over a date window. |
| [`corporate-actions show`](#corporate-actions-show) | Read | Every field of one Alpaca corporate action, looked up in Market Data and then Trading API announcements. |
| [`crypto bars`](#crypto-bars) | Read | OHLCV bars for a crypto pair from Alpaca's US crypto feed (times in ET). |
| [`crypto buy`](#crypto-buy) | Money | Buy a crypto pair (fractional, GTC/IOC) through the TransactionGateway. Paper by default; live needs a confirmation code. |
| [`crypto fee-estimate`](#crypto-fee-estimate) | Read | Alpaca's network fee estimate for sending a coin to an address (read-only, nothing is sent). |
| [`crypto latest`](#crypto-latest) | Read | The latest trade, quote and minute bar for a crypto pair. |
| [`crypto orderbook`](#crypto-orderbook) | Read | The latest order book for a crypto pair: bids and asks side by side. |
| [`crypto positions`](#crypto-positions) | Read | Your crypto holdings in the Alpaca paper and live accounts: quantity, cost, price, unrealized P&L. |
| [`crypto quotes`](#crypto-quotes) | Read | Recent best bid/ask quotes for a crypto pair, with the spread. |
| [`crypto sell`](#crypto-sell) | Money | Sell crypto you hold (crypto is long-only). Exits always clear the gates; live needs a confirmation code. |
| [`crypto snapshot`](#crypto-snapshot) | Read | Snapshot of a crypto pair: latest trade and quote, minute bar, today's and the prior daily bar. |
| [`crypto trades`](#crypto-trades) | Read | Recent trade prints for a crypto pair (price, size, taker side). |
| [`crypto transfers`](#crypto-transfers) | Read | Crypto deposits and withdrawals on your Alpaca accounts: status, amount, fees, addresses (ET). |
| [`crypto wallets`](#crypto-wallets) | Read | Your Alpaca crypto deposit wallets (address per coin) on paper and live; fails closed when funding is not enabled. |
| [`crypto whitelist`](#crypto-whitelist) | Read | Addresses your Alpaca accounts may withdraw crypto to, with their approval status. |
| [`crypto whitelist-add`](#crypto-whitelist-add) | Money | Ask Alpaca to whitelist a withdrawal address. Always previews and needs a confirmation code. |
| [`crypto whitelist-remove`](#crypto-whitelist-remove) | Write | Remove a whitelisted withdrawal address. Always previews and needs a confirmation code. |
| [`crypto withdraw`](#crypto-withdraw) | Money | Send coins from your Alpaca account to a whitelisted address. Always previews and needs a confirmation code. |
| [`dataset export`](#dataset-export) | Write | Export the replay feature store as ML-ready CSVs (trades.csv, bars.csv, manifest.json), backfilling older runs first. |
| [`diary export`](#diary-export) | Write | Export your trade diary to a CSV file (ET times, P&L, risk plan, R), or print it with --csv -. |
| [`diary list`](#diary-list) | Read | Your trade diary, newest first: entry/exit, mode, size, exit reason and realized P&L. |
| [`diary pnl`](#diary-pnl) | Read | Realized P&L from closed trades per day, week or month (ET), optionally by strategy or symbol. |
| [`diary show`](#diary-show) | Read | One diary trade in full: entry, exit, order ids, the risk plan that managed it, P&L and R. |
| [`diary stats`](#diary-stats) | Read | Trading performance from the diary: win rate, expectancy, profit factor, avg R, MFE/MAE, drawdown. |
| [`docs dsl`](#docs-dsl) | Read | Explain one IdiotScript verb: phase, signatures, meaning, doc comment, an example from its real signature, and uses. |
| [`docs explain`](#docs-explain) | Read | Explain a type or member: its doc comment, where it is declared (path:line), its members and its callers. |
| [`docs law`](#docs-law) | Read | Show one BIBLE law (IP-LAW-n) in full, or list every law. |
| [`docs search`](#docs-search) | Read | Search everything IdiotProof knows about itself: BIBLE, docs, stories, tickets, code docs and catalogs. |
| [`docs section`](#docs-section) | Read | Show one BIBLE section (IP-§n, subsections included), or the table of contents. |
| [`docs story`](#docs-story) | Read | Show one user story (IP-US-*) with its status and proving tests, or list an epic's stories. |
| [`docs ticket`](#docs-ticket) | Read | Show one ticket: status, description, requires / required-by, the commits that name it, and its history. |
| [`dsl format`](#dsl-format) | Read | Render canonical strategy JSON (or a stamp) as IdiotScript text, checking it parses back to the same strategy. |
| [`dsl glossary`](#dsl-glossary) | Read | Plain-English meaning of IdiotScript verbs: every entry, or one verb (aliases resolve). |
| [`dsl parse`](#dsl-parse) | Read | Parse IdiotScript (or JSON or a stamp) into the canonical strategy JSON the Monitor evaluates; nothing is saved. |
| [`dsl validate`](#dsl-validate) | Read | Validate IdiotScript/JSON against the phase rules and the gates, failing closed with every reason (nothing is saved). |
| [`dsl verbs`](#dsl-verbs) | Read | The IdiotScript verb catalog by phase, reflected from the code that compiles it (IP-LAW-4). |
| [`gapper apply-tuned`](#gapper-apply-tuned) | Write | Save a backtest's hindsight-tuned profile as a new gapper strategy (inactive unless --arm). |
| [`gapper arm`](#gapper-arm) | Money | Arm a gapper: activate an existing one or queue a new one from a profile, honoring one-per-symbol and the 3-gapper cap. |
| [`gapper auto candidates`](#gapper-auto-candidates) | Read | Every ticker an auto-gapper scan screened on a day: signals, the adaptive plan it chose, and armed or why skipped. |
| [`gapper auto disable`](#gapper-auto-disable) | Write | Disarm every auto-armed gapper of yours that holds no position (holding ones stay armed to manage their exit). |
| [`gapper auto enable`](#gapper-auto-enable) | Write | Run the auto-gapper for you now and arm its top picks as paper gappers (paper-only; --dry-run previews). |
| [`gapper auto status`](#gapper-auto-status) | Read | Auto-gapper settings, its recent scans (screened, qualified, armed, skipped) and your auto-armed gappers. |
| [`gapper backtest-day`](#gapper-backtest-day) | Read | Replay a gapper profile over one past day: fills, MFE/MAE, the giveback grid and a hindsight-tuned profile (saved for apply-tuned). |
| [`gapper be-bex status`](#gapper-be-bex-status) | Read | The BE/BEX decay gate: latest decay reading, threshold, and which gated BE strategies are armed or disarmed by it. |
| [`gapper caps`](#gapper-caps) | Read | Active-gapper counts against the caps: 3 manual gappers, one active strategy per symbol, the auto-gapper limit. |
| [`gapper disarm`](#gapper-disarm) | Write | Disarm a gapper so the Monitor stops evaluating it (refused while it holds a position); --remove deletes it. |
| [`gapper from-transcript`](#gapper-from-transcript) | Read | Read a transcript and propose re-validated gapper candidate cards; nothing is queued until you `gapper arm` one. |
| [`gapper list`](#gapper-list) | Read | Your queued gappers with live state: armed, mode, position, condition progress and last exit. |
| [`gapper premarket-fade`](#gapper-premarket-fade) | Read | Premarket blow-off/fade detector: `run` scans the movers now (detection only), `status` lists today's fade alerts. |
| [`gapper profile show`](#gapper-profile-show) | Read | Every dial of one gapper profile, plus the strategy it generates for a sample ticker. |
| [`gapper profiles`](#gapper-profiles) | Read | List the gapper profile catalog: the templates every gapper starts from. |
| [`gapper tune`](#gapper-tune) | Write | Dial a gapper profile in for one ticker and show the strategy GapperScriptFactory generates; --save stores it inactive. |
| [`hub install-service`](#hub-install-service) | Destructive | Install the Hub as a Windows service that runs as you (Monitor off unless --monitor). |
| [`hub ping`](#hub-ping) | Read | Check the Hub is up and show its clock in ET. |
| [`hub uninstall-service`](#hub-uninstall-service) | Destructive | Stop and remove the Hub's Windows service. |
| [`indicators compute`](#indicators-compute) | Read | Compute one indicator (rsi, ema, atr, macd, vwap, adx, bollinger, ...) on a symbol's recent bars. |
| [`indicators snapshot`](#indicators-snapshot) | Read | The full indicator snapshot a strategy condition sees for a symbol: VWAP, EMAs, RSI, MACD, ADX, gap, window high/low, pivots, patterns. |
| [`keys migrate-to-vault`](#keys-migrate-to-vault) | Destructive | Move Alpaca keys, OAuth tokens and Claude keys out of SQL into MindAttic.Vault (dry run unless --apply). |
| [`keys opt-in`](#keys-opt-in) | Write | Route your orders to your own Alpaca account (alpaca) or back to the Sandbox (off). |
| [`keys probe`](#keys-probe) | Read | Round-trip your stored Alpaca keys with a read-only account call (paper, live or both). |
| [`keys set`](#keys-set) | Write | Store an Alpaca paper/live key pair (checked, then probed) or your Claude key in MindAttic.Vault. |
| [`keys status`](#keys-status) | Read | Which Alpaca/Claude keys resolve for you and from which Vault entry (never shows a secret). |
| [`ledger list`](#ledger-list) | Read | Every command the Hub ran for you (CLI, MCP, web): operation, arguments, outcome, duration (ET). |
| [`llm keys`](#llm-keys) | Read | Which Claude key the LLM panel resolves for you (yours, the host's, or none) and the voting toggles; never shows a key. |
| [`llm panel`](#llm-panel) | Read | The LLM voter panel: voters, trading lenses, which have keys, the consensus threshold and whether the gate is on. |
| [`llm threshold`](#llm-threshold) | Write | Show or set the LLM panel's consensus threshold (0.5-1): the share of votes that must Approve. |
| [`llm vote`](#llm-vote) | Read | Dry-run the LLM voter panel on a strategy's current entry: every vote and the consensus. Never places an order. |
| [`llm voting disable`](#llm-voting-disable) | Write | Turn off your own LLM voter gate (a host-wide setting still applies). |
| [`llm voting enable`](#llm-voting-enable) | Write | Turn on the LLM voter gate for your automated entries (needs a Claude key to take effect). |
| [`market auctions`](#market-auctions) | Read | Opening and closing auction prices and sizes per day for one or more stocks (SIP, times in ET). |
| [`market bars`](#market-bars) | Read | Historical OHLCV bars for a stock at any timeframe, oldest first (times in ET). |
| [`market bond-prices`](#market-bond-prices) | Read | Latest Alpaca fixed income prices and yields for the given ISINs. |
| [`market candlesticks`](#market-candlesticks) | Read | Candlestick patterns (engulfing, hammer, shooting star, doji) on a symbol's recent bars. |
| [`market chart`](#market-chart) | Read | ASCII candle chart of a symbol across premarket, regular and after-hours sessions (ET); crypto pairs as 24h days. |
| [`market conditions`](#market-conditions) | Read | What each trade or quote condition code means (the codes in market trades/quotes). |
| [`market exchanges`](#market-exchanges) | Read | Exchange codes used in trades and quotes and the venue each one names. |
| [`market feed status`](#market-feed-status) | Read | The Hub's market data feed: Alpaca SIP/IEX or Mock, whether it can switch, and active strategies per mode. |
| [`market feed switch`](#market-feed-switch) | Write | Switch the Hub's market data to sip, iex or mock (mock refused while Paper/Live strategies are active). |
| [`market fx`](#market-fx) | Read | Latest forex rates (bid/mid/ask) or historical rate bars for currency pairs (times in ET). |
| [`market latest`](#market-latest) | Read | Latest minute bar, trade or quote for one or more stocks (times in ET). |
| [`market logo`](#market-logo) | Write | Download a company's logo and save it under %LOCALAPPDATA%\MindAttic\IdiotProof\Logos; reports the path and size. |
| [`market meta`](#market-meta) | Read | All market-data reference codes at once: exchanges plus trade and quote conditions. |
| [`market most-actives`](#market-most-actives) | Read | Today's most active stocks by share volume or trade count (Alpaca screener). |
| [`market movers`](#market-movers) | Read | Today's top stock gainers and losers by percent change (Alpaca screener). |
| [`market news`](#market-news) | Read | Latest news headlines for one or more stocks, or the whole market (times in ET). |
| [`market prev-close`](#market-prev-close) | Read | Previous session's close (and full daily bar) for one or more stocks, with the move since. |
| [`market quote`](#market-quote) | Read | Latest trade and bid/ask for one or more stocks (Alpaca market data, times in ET). |
| [`market quotes`](#market-quotes) | Read | Historical bid/ask quotes for a stock: sizes, exchanges, spread (times in ET). |
| [`market scan-universe`](#market-scan-universe) | Read | Screen the tracked ticker universe on live price, volume and % change (Alpaca snapshots); arms nothing. |
| [`market snapshot`](#market-snapshot) | Read | One-line snapshot per stock: last, change vs prior close, bid/ask, today's open/high/low/volume. |
| [`market trades`](#market-trades) | Read | Historical trade prints for a stock: price, size, exchange, conditions (times in ET). |
| [`monitor heartbeat`](#monitor-heartbeat) | Read | The Monitor loop's last heartbeat: when it ticked, ok or fail, failures in a row. |
| [`monitor lease`](#monitor-lease) | Read | Who holds the Monitor's SQL leader lease (only the holder evaluates and trades). |
| [`monitor pause`](#monitor-pause) | Write | Pause the Monitor: from its next tick it evaluates nothing - no entries and NO exits - until resumed. |
| [`monitor resume`](#monitor-resume) | Money | Resume a paused Monitor (needs a confirmation code when a Live strategy is active). |
| [`monitor status`](#monitor-status) | Read | Is the Monitor trading? Hosted, lease, last tick, paused, window, active strategies. |
| [`monitor tail`](#monitor-tail) | Read | Recent Monitor activity: gate verdicts (fire, veto, block, entry, exit, reject) and live condition progress. |
| [`monitor tick-once`](#monitor-tick-once) | Read | Run one evaluation pass over your active strategies and show each verdict - never places, cancels or records an order. |
| [`options bars`](#options-bars) | Read | Historical OHLCV bars for one option contract. |
| [`options buy`](#options-buy) | Money | Buy option contracts to open (level 2+). Sandbox by default; live needs a confirmation code. |
| [`options chain`](#options-chain) | Read | An underlying's option chain for one expiration: calls and puts by strike with bid/ask, IV, delta and open interest. |
| [`options close`](#options-close) | Money | Close a whole options position (sells a long, buys back a short) through the gateway. |
| [`options conditions`](#options-conditions) | Read | Options trade or quote condition codes and what they mean. |
| [`options contract`](#options-contract) | Read | Full catalog details of one option contract by OCC symbol or Alpaca id. |
| [`options contracts`](#options-contracts) | Read | Search listed option contracts for an underlying by expiry, type, strike range and status. |
| [`options do-not-exercise`](#options-do-not-exercise) | Money | Opt a held contract out of automatic exercise at expiry (paper or live; live needs a code). |
| [`options exchanges`](#options-exchanges) | Read | Options exchange codes and their names, as they appear in quotes and trades. |
| [`options exercise`](#options-exercise) | Money | Exercise a long option you hold (Alpaca paper or live; live needs a confirmation code). |
| [`options glossary`](#options-glossary) | Read | Plain-English options jargon (hype, breakeven, IV, sell to close, ...): every term, or one in full. |
| [`options greeks`](#options-greeks) | Read | Delta, gamma, theta, vega and rho for one option contract; badged Model when computed locally. |
| [`options iv`](#options-iv) | Read | Implied volatility for one option contract: Alpaca's, plus IV solved locally at bid, mid, ask and last. |
| [`options latest`](#options-latest) | Read | Latest NBBO quote and latest trade for one option contract, with exchanges and sizes. |
| [`options level`](#options-level) | Read | Options trading level (effective and approved) and options buying power for your Alpaca accounts. |
| [`options positions`](#options-positions) | Read | Open option contracts in your Alpaca accounts: strike, expiry, DTE, cost, value and unrealized P&L. |
| [`options quote`](#options-quote) | Read | Latest bid/ask, mid, spread and last trade for one option contract (OCC symbol). |
| [`options sell`](#options-sell) | Money | Sell option contracts you hold (sell to close), or write them with --open (level 1+). |
| [`options signals`](#options-signals) | Read | Sell-the-hype nudges on your open long options: hype near its session high plus bullish news (never places anything). |
| [`options snapshot`](#options-snapshot) | Read | Alpaca's full snapshot of one option contract: latest quote and trade, daily bars, IV and Greeks. |
| [`options spread`](#options-spread) | Money | Place a 2-4 leg options order (verticals, straddles, ratios...) as one Alpaca multi-leg order; level 3, max-loss preview, live needs a code. |
| [`options trades`](#options-trades) | Read | Historical trades (prints) for one option contract, newest first. |
| [`options value`](#options-value) | Read | Intrinsic and extrinsic value, breakeven, DTE and Black-Scholes price for one option contract. |
| [`orders bracket`](#orders-bracket) | Money | Entry plus a take-profit and a stop-loss that cancel each other (Alpaca bracket). The stop-loss is the Risk Guardian's stop. |
| [`orders cancel`](#orders-cancel) | Money | Cancel one working order through the gateway (audited; live needs a confirmation code). |
| [`orders cancel-all`](#orders-cancel-all) | Money | Cancel every open order in an account, or only one symbol's, through the gateway (live needs a confirmation code). |
| [`orders history`](#orders-history) | Read | Closed Alpaca orders (filled, cancelled, expired, rejected) over the last N days, newest first, with fill prices and totals. |
| [`orders list`](#orders-list) | Read | Your Alpaca orders (open by default) in the paper and live accounts, newest first, with bracket/OCO legs. |
| [`orders oco`](#orders-oco) | Money | Exit a held position with a take-profit limit and a stop-loss; whichever fills cancels the other (Alpaca OCO). |
| [`orders oto`](#orders-oto) | Money | Entry that, once filled, triggers ONE child: a take-profit or a stop-loss (Alpaca OTO). |
| [`orders place`](#orders-place) | Money | Place any single Alpaca order: market/limit/stop/stop-limit/trailing, every TIF, fractional or notional, client id, position intent. Through the gateway; live needs a code. |
| [`orders replace`](#orders-replace) | Money | Change a working order's quantity, limit/stop/trail, TIF or client id (Alpaca PATCH; it gets a new id). Through the gateway; live needs a code. |
| [`orders show`](#orders-show) | Read | One Alpaca order in full, by id or client id: prices, fills, timestamps (ET) and its nested bracket/OCO/OTO/multi-leg legs. |
| [`positions close`](#positions-close) | Money | Close (or trim) one Alpaca position as a market exit through the TransactionGateway. Live needs a confirmation code. |
| [`positions close-all`](#positions-close-all) | Money | Close every Alpaca position in one account with market exits through the TransactionGateway; optionally cancel open orders first. Live needs a confirmation code. |
| [`positions list`](#positions-list) | Read | Every open position in your Alpaca paper and live accounts: price, today's move, unrealized P&L. |
| [`positions reconcile`](#positions-reconcile) | Read | Read-only report: what Alpaca actually holds vs what your strategies book (PositionQty), per account. |
| [`positions show`](#positions-show) | Read | One position in your Alpaca paper/live accounts, the IdiotProof strategy that owns it, and its latest trade-diary row. |
| [`prefs get`](#prefs-get) | Read | Show your preferences: theme, account pill and Risk Guardian limits. |
| [`prefs set`](#prefs-set) | Write | Change one of your preferences (risk limits keep the Settings page's sanity rules). |
| [`replay all`](#replay-all) | Write | Replay every strategy family on one ticker/day and rank them by realized P&L (best fit first). |
| [`replay compare`](#replay-compare) | Read | Two replay runs side by side: strategy, day, fires, round-trips, win rate, hold time and P&L, with the difference. |
| [`replay families`](#replay-families) | Read | The built-in strategy families `replay run --family` and `replay all` use, with what each trades. |
| [`replay list`](#replay-list) | Read | The replay archive, newest first: ticker, day, strategy, sim or live, fired and P&L. |
| [`replay live`](#replay-live) | Write | Render the Monitor's real trades for a day (from the trade diary) on that day's bars as LIVE runs in the archive. |
| [`replay regen`](#replay-regen) | Write | Regenerate the replay archive's HTML (every run page and index) from SQL; never uploads or deploys. |
| [`replay run`](#replay-run) | Write | Replay a strategy, gapper profile or built-in family over one past day with the Monitor's own evaluator; saves the run and its page. |
| [`replay show`](#replay-show) | Read | One replay run: its round-trips with entry features and its per-bar features (OHLCV, VWAP, volume ratio, conditions passed). |
| [`research analyze`](#research-analyze) | Write | Extract catalysts and portents from a ticker's news, a URL or pasted text via the LLM (--save to keep them). |
| [`research backfill`](#research-backfill) | Write | Record what each old enough claim's stock actually did (Alpaca daily closes) and settle portents. |
| [`research claim`](#research-claim) | Read | One research claim in full: source, trigger, outcome, insider lines and its score breakdown. |
| [`research claims`](#research-claims) | Read | Ranked research feed: catalysts and portents by significance score, filterable by ticker, date, score and macro. |
| [`research index-events`](#research-index-events) | Read | S&P 500 / S&P 100 additions and removals: announced and effective dates, pending or done. |
| [`research insiders`](#research-insiders) | Read | Form 4 insider transactions for a ticker: filer, role, buy/sell, shares, price, value. |
| [`research macro`](#research-macro) | Read | Macro and regulatory claims (rule changes, listing standards) with the tickers each affects. |
| [`research scan`](#research-scan) | Write | Run one research scan pass now in the Hub (news, SEC filings, regulatory, index events, backfill, scoring). |
| [`research score`](#research-score) | Read | Explain a claim's 0-100 significance score term by term (magnitude, confidence, history, source, watchlist, recency). |
| [`research similar`](#research-similar) | Read | Look-alike past claims (LSH neighbours) and what their stocks did afterwards. |
| [`research ticker`](#research-ticker) | Read | Everything research knows about one ticker: claims, portents, macro and index events, insiders, outcomes. |
| [`research universe list`](#research-universe-list) | Read | The tracked ticker universe the research scan sweeps: symbol, exchange, last price, freshness. |
| [`research universe refresh`](#research-universe-refresh) | Write | Reload the tracked ticker universe (asset list and last prices) from Alpaca when stale, or --force. |
| [`risk check`](#risk-check) | Read | Dry-run a setup through your Risk Guardian: approved or why not, worst case, and the largest size allowed. Places nothing. |
| [`risk kill-switch`](#risk-kill-switch) | Write | Halt every new entry now (on), or resume (off, which needs a confirmation code); exits always go through. |
| [`risk set`](#risk-set) | Write | Change Risk Guardian limits; unnamed ones keep their value and today's loss counter is preserved. |
| [`risk show`](#risk-show) | Read | Your six Risk Guardian limits (per-trade and daily loss, stop range, balance, account risk %) and the kill switch. |
| [`risk status`](#risk-status) | Read | Today's realized P&L, losses counted against the daily breaker, remaining room, breaker and kill-switch state. |
| [`scan movers`](#scan-movers) | Write | Screen today's top gainers to the gapper band; --replay replays each survivor with a gapper profile and saves the runs. |
| [`settings get`](#settings-get) | Read | Show one runtime setting: value, default, range and meaning. |
| [`settings list`](#settings-list) | Read | List the app's runtime settings with current value, default, range and meaning. |
| [`settings set`](#settings-set) | Write | Change one runtime setting (type- and range-checked; unknown and internal keys refused). |
| [`strategy activate`](#strategy-activate) | Money | Hand a strategy to the Monitor. A Live strategy needs a confirmation code. |
| [`strategy bulk`](#strategy-bulk) | Money | Activate or deactivate many strategies at once (--all, --symbol, --mode). Live activations need one confirmation code for the batch. |
| [`strategy clone`](#strategy-clone) | Write | Copy a strategy (optionally onto another symbol) as a new, inactive Sandbox strategy. |
| [`strategy create`](#strategy-create) | Write | Create a strategy from IdiotScript or canonical JSON after validating it. It starts inactive in Sandbox. |
| [`strategy deactivate`](#strategy-deactivate) | Write | Stop the Monitor evaluating a strategy (refused while it holds a position). |
| [`strategy delete`](#strategy-delete) | Destructive | Soft-delete a strategy: deactivate it and mark it [deleted] (reversible with --restore). Refused while it holds a position. |
| [`strategy diff`](#strategy-diff) | Read | Compare two strategies field by field at the canon level (what the Monitor actually runs), plus title, mode and state. |
| [`strategy explain`](#strategy-explain) | Read | Explain a strategy in plain English, phase by phase — generated from its canon, no LLM, the same words every time. |
| [`strategy export`](#strategy-export) | Read | Export a strategy as a stamp, armored payload, canonical JSON or IdiotScript. |
| [`strategy fires`](#strategy-fires) | Read | Why a strategy did or didn't fire: its recent gate verdicts (conditions met, LLM veto, Risk Guardian block, order placed or rejected) and where it stands now. |
| [`strategy from-text`](#strategy-from-text) | Write | Turn a plain-English description into a strategy (via the LLM), show its stamp, and save it only when you confirm. |
| [`strategy from-watchlist`](#strategy-from-watchlist) | Write | Create one strategy per item of a watchlist JSON file (the Monitor's create-strategies, through the CLI). |
| [`strategy history`](#strategy-history) | Read | A strategy's trail, newest first: Monitor verdicts and fills, diary trades, and the CLI/MCP commands that touched it. |
| [`strategy import`](#strategy-import) | Write | Create a strategy from a stamp, canonical JSON or IdiotScript. It starts inactive in Sandbox. |
| [`strategy list`](#strategy-list) | Read | List your strategies with mode, position and live condition progress. |
| [`strategy mode`](#strategy-mode) | Money | Route a strategy to sandbox, paper or live. Switching to live needs a confirmation code. |
| [`strategy progress`](#strategy-progress) | Read | How close a strategy is to firing: conditions passing N/M, the first failing verb and the last price, optionally watched. |
| [`strategy quarantine`](#strategy-quarantine) | Read | List strategies the Monitor refuses to evaluate (canon unreadable, or no canon and a script that doesn't parse), with the reason. |
| [`strategy rename`](#strategy-rename) | Write | Give a strategy a new title. Its canon, stamp id and state are untouched. |
| [`strategy resync-canon`](#strategy-resync-canon) | Write | Re-derive your strategies' canons from their scripts where the script now yields a richer canon; dry run unless --apply. |
| [`strategy samples`](#strategy-samples) | Read | List the built-in sample strategies, or show one as IdiotScript, a stamp or canonical JSON. |
| [`strategy set`](#strategy-set) | Money | Edit a strategy's stop, target, trailing, size, sell-by time or session; the canon is rewritten and re-validated. |
| [`strategy show`](#strategy-show) | Read | Everything about one strategy: settings, script, position, progress. |
| [`strategy stamp`](#strategy-stamp) | Read | Print the strategy's ASCII stamp: header, phase flow, exit ladder, fingerprint and a paste-back payload. |
| [`strategy validate`](#strategy-validate) | Read | Check a saved strategy or a script: parse, canon round-trip, phase rules and a risk preview. Changes nothing. |
| [`trade buy`](#trade-buy) | Money | Buy shares (open or add to a long). Sandbox by default; live needs a confirmation code. |
| [`trade confirm`](#trade-confirm) | Money | Execute a pending Live order by its confirmation code (exactly what was previewed, once). |
| [`trade cover`](#trade-cover) | Money | Buy to cover a short. |
| [`trade flatten`](#trade-flatten) | Money | Flatten a symbol, a strategy's position, or the whole account with market exits through the TransactionGateway. Live needs a confirmation code. |
| [`trade notional`](#trade-notional) | Money | Buy (or sell) a dollar amount of a stock: a fractional, DAY, market order sized in dollars. Live needs a code. |
| [`trade pending`](#trade-pending) | Read | List Live confirmations still waiting for a yes. |
| [`trade preview`](#trade-preview) | Read | Run every gate on an order without placing it (no code issued). |
| [`trade sell`](#trade-sell) | Money | Sell shares you hold (close or trim a long). Exits always clear the gates. |
| [`trade short`](#trade-short) | Money | Sell short (open a short). Needs a stop above entry; margin + shortable name at the broker. |
| [`users create`](#users-create) | Write | Create an IdiotProof account (blocklist and password rules of web sign-up; Argon2id via MindAttic.Authentication). |
| [`users list`](#users-list) | Read | List the IdiotProof accounts (test fixtures hidden unless --all); * marks who you act as. |
| [`watchlist add`](#watchlist-add) | Write | Add symbols to your IdiotProof watchlist (creates a 'Main' workspace when you have none). |
| [`watchlist list`](#watchlist-list) | Read | Your IdiotProof watchlist: the symbols on each of your workspaces (not Alpaca's watchlists). |
| [`watchlist remove`](#watchlist-remove) | Write | Remove symbols from your IdiotProof watchlist. |
| [`watchlists add`](#watchlists-add) | Write | Add symbols to an Alpaca watchlist (by id or name). |
| [`watchlists create`](#watchlists-create) | Write | Create an Alpaca watchlist, optionally with symbols. |
| [`watchlists delete`](#watchlists-delete) | Destructive | Delete an Alpaca watchlist (by id or name). |
| [`watchlists list`](#watchlists-list) | Read | Your Alpaca server-side watchlists (not IdiotProof's local watchlist): name, id, last update. |
| [`watchlists remove`](#watchlists-remove) | Write | Remove symbols from an Alpaca watchlist (by id or name). |
| [`watchlists rename`](#watchlists-rename) | Write | Rename an Alpaca watchlist, keeping its symbols. |
| [`watchlists show`](#watchlists-show) | Read | One Alpaca watchlist (by id or name) and its symbols. |

## account

### account activities

```text
Account activity log: fills, dividends, fees, deposits, interest, option expirations/assignments (newest first, ET).

Usage: idiotproof account activities [--since <date>] [--until <date>] [--type <string[]>] [--limit <int>] [--mode <all|paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --since <date>           First ET date to include, yyyy-MM-dd (default: 7 days ago).
      --until <date>           Last ET date to include, yyyy-MM-dd (default: today).
      --type <string[]>        Activity types, comma-separated: FILL, DIV, FEE, CSD (deposit), CSW (withdrawal), JNLC, INT, OPEXP, OPASN, ... (default: all).
      --limit <int>            Most rows per account, newest first (default 100, max 1000). (default: 100)
      --mode <all|paper|live>  paper, live or all (default all). (default: all)

Examples:
  idiotproof account activities
  idiotproof account activities --since 2026-10-01 --type FILL --mode paper
  idiotproof account activities --type DIV,FEE,INT
```

### account buying-power

```text
Buying power by kind (overall, Reg T, day-trading, non-marginable, options), cash and margin multiplier.

Usage: idiotproof account buying-power [--mode <all|paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --mode <all|paper|live>  paper, live or all (default all). (default: all)

Examples:
  idiotproof account buying-power
  idiotproof account buying-power --mode live
```

### account calendar

```text
Trading days with premarket, regular and after-hours times (ET); early closes and holidays called out.

Usage: idiotproof account calendar [--from <date>] [--to <date>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --from <date>                First date, yyyy-MM-dd (default today ET).
      --to <date>                  Last date, yyyy-MM-dd (default 14 days after --from).
      --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Which Alpaca account's keys ask: paper or live (default paper; the calendar is the same). (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof account calendar
  idiotproof account calendar --from 2026-11-20 --to 2026-12-31
```

### account clock

```text
Is the market open now, and when it next opens and closes (ET), from Alpaca's clock.

Usage: idiotproof account clock [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Which Alpaca account's keys ask: paper or live (default paper; the clock is the same). (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof account clock
```

### account config

```text
Alpaca account settings side by side: DTBP/PDT checks, shorting, fractional, margin cap, options level, trade suspension.

Usage: idiotproof account config [--mode <all|paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --mode <all|paper|live>  paper, live or all (default all). (default: all)

Examples:
  idiotproof account config
  idiotproof account config --mode live
```

### account config set

```text
Change one Alpaca account setting (Live needs a confirmation code).

Usage: idiotproof account config set <setting> <value> [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <setting>                        dtbp_check, pdt_check, trade_confirm_email, suspend_trade, no_shorting, fractional_trading, max_margin_multiplier, max_options_trading_level or ptp_no_exception_entry. (required)
  <value>                          The new value (see `account config` for each setting's meaning). (required)
      --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  paper or live (default paper; live needs a confirmation code). (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof account config set no_shorting true
  idiotproof account config set max_margin_multiplier 1 --mode live
```

### account history

```text
Equity over time as a Braille line chart, with the true P&L (deposits excluded) for 1D to all-time windows.

Usage: idiotproof account history [--period <string>] [--timeframe <string>] [--extended] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--width <int>] [--height <int>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --period <string>            Window: <n>D, <n>W, <n>M or <n>A (years), or all (default 1M). (default: 1M)
      --timeframe <string>         Point spacing: 1Min, 5Min, 15Min, 1H or 1D (default: Alpaca's choice for the period).
      --extended                   Include premarket and after-hours in intraday history (default regular hours only). (default: false)
      --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  paper or live (default paper). (default: paper)
      --width <int>                Chart width in characters (default: the terminal's, else 118).
      --height <int>               Chart rows (default 16). (default: 16)

Examples:
  idiotproof account history
  idiotproof account history --period 1D --timeframe 5Min --extended
  idiotproof account history --period 1A --mode live
```

### account pdt

```text
Pattern-day-trader standing: day trades in the last 5 business days, PDT flag, equity vs the $25k floor, trades left.

Usage: idiotproof account pdt [--mode <all|paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --mode <all|paper|live>  paper, live or all (default all). (default: all)

Examples:
  idiotproof account pdt
  idiotproof account pdt --mode live
```

### account summary

```text
Equity, cash, buying power and today's true P&L (deposits excluded) for your Alpaca paper and live accounts.

Usage: idiotproof account summary [--mode <all|paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:

  idiotproof account summary --mode live
```

## assets

### assets bonds

```text
Alpaca fixed income assets: US Treasuries or US corporate bonds with coupon, maturity, last close and yield.

Usage: idiotproof assets bonds [--type <treasuries|corporates>] [--subtype <string>] [--bond-status <string>] [--cusips <string[]>] [--isins <string[]>] [--search <string>] [--limit <int>] [--mode <paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --type <treasuries|corporates>  treasuries (default) or corporates. (default: treasuries)
      --subtype <string>              Treasury subtype filter (bill, note, bond, strips, tips, floating_rate).
      --bond-status <string>          Bond status filter (outstanding, matured, pre_issuance).
      --cusips <string[]>             Only these CUSIPs, comma separated.
      --isins <string[]>              Only these ISINs, comma separated.
      --search <string>               Keep bonds whose description, issuer, ticker, CUSIP or ISIN contains this text.
      --limit <int>                   Rows to show (default 50; sorted by maturity). (default: 50)
      --mode <paper|live>             Alpaca account to ask: paper (default) or live. (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof assets bonds --subtype bill --limit 20
  idiotproof assets bonds --type corporates --search AAPL
```

### assets list

```text
Alpaca's tradable universe (/v2/assets) filtered by class, exchange, status and attributes, with totals.

Alpaca returns 10k+ assets; this shows the first --limit matches (sorted by symbol) and how many matched in all.

Usage: idiotproof assets list [--class <us-equity|us-option|crypto>] [--exchange <string>] [--status <active|inactive|all>] [--attributes <string[]>] [--search <string>] [--tradable] [--shortable] [--limit <int>] [--mode <paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --class <us-equity|us-option|crypto>  us_equity, us_option or crypto (default: every class).
      --exchange <string>                   Only this exchange (NASDAQ, NYSE, ARCA, AMEX, BATS, OTC, CRYPTO...).
      --status <active|inactive|all>        active, inactive or all (default active). (default: active)
      --attributes <string[]>               Alpaca attribute filter, comma separated (ptp_no_exception, ptp_with_exception, ipo, has_options, options_late_close, fractional_eh_enabled...).
      --search <string>                     Keep assets whose symbol starts with, or name contains, this text.
      --tradable                            Only assets tradable at Alpaca. (default: false)
      --shortable                           Only shortable assets. (default: false)
      --limit <int>                         Rows to show (default 50; the totals line counts them all). (default: 50)
      --mode <paper|live>                   Alpaca account to ask: paper (default) or live. (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof assets list --class us_equity --exchange NASDAQ --search APP
  idiotproof assets list --class crypto --limit 100
  idiotproof assets list --attributes has_options --shortable
```

### assets show

```text
One Alpaca asset: tradable, shortable, easy-to-borrow, marginable, fractionable and margin requirements.

Usage: idiotproof assets show <symbol> [--mode <paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <symbol>                 Ticker, crypto pair (BTC/USD) or Alpaca asset id. (required)
      --mode <paper|live>  Alpaca account to ask: paper (default) or live. (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof assets show AAPL
  idiotproof assets show BTC/USD
```

## audit

### audit list

```text
The audit trail, newest first: signals, entries/exits, rejections, risk blocks, system events (ET).

Usage: idiotproof audit list [--since <date>] [--kind <string[]>] [--system] [--limit <int>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --since <date>     First ET date to include, yyyy-MM-dd (default: everything kept).
      --kind <string[]>  Only these categories, comma-separated: signal-fire, entry, exit, order-rejected, risk, broker, system, ...
      --system           Include system-wide rows that belong to no user (default on; --no-system for only yours). (default: true)
      --limit <int>      Most rows, newest first, 1-1000 (default 50). (default: 50)

Examples:
  idiotproof audit list
  idiotproof audit list --since 2026-10-30 --kind signal-fire,entry,exit
  idiotproof audit list --kind order-rejected --no-system --limit 200
```

### audit search

```text
Find audit rows whose message or payload contains text: a symbol, order id, strategy title.

Usage: idiotproof audit search <text> [--since <date>] [--kind <string[]>] [--system] [--limit <int>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <text>                 Text to find in the message or the structured payload (case-insensitive). (required)
      --since <date>     First ET date to include, yyyy-MM-dd (default: everything kept).
      --kind <string[]>  Only these categories, comma-separated: signal-fire, entry, exit, order-rejected, risk, broker, system, ...
      --system           Include system-wide rows that belong to no user (default on; --no-system for only yours). (default: true)
      --limit <int>      Most rows, newest first, 1-1000 (default 50). (default: 50)

Examples:
  idiotproof audit search NVDA
  idiotproof audit search "insufficient buying power" --since 2026-10-01
```

### audit tail

```text
The latest audit rows, oldest first; --follow watches for new ones for a bounded time (--seconds, --max).

Usage: idiotproof audit tail [--lines <int>] [--follow] [--seconds <int>] [--max <int>] [--kind <string[]>] [--system]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  -n, --lines <int>      How many of the latest rows to start with, 0-500 (default 20). (default: 20)
  -f, --follow           Keep watching for new rows until --seconds pass or --max new rows arrive. (default: false)
      --seconds <int>    With --follow: how long to watch, 1-300 (default 30). (default: 30)
      --max <int>        With --follow: stop after this many new rows, 1-1000 (default 200). (default: 200)
      --kind <string[]>  Only these categories, comma-separated.
      --system           Include system-wide rows (default on; --no-system for only yours). (default: true)

Examples:
  idiotproof audit tail
  idiotproof audit tail --follow --seconds 60 --kind signal-fire,entry,exit
```

## backtest

### backtest conditions

```text
A backtest day's per-candle condition table: each entry condition's truth per bar, fires, entries and time in position.

Usage: idiotproof backtest conditions <run> [--date <date>] [--all]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <run>              The run id `backtest run` printed (bt-xxxxxxxx). (required)
  -d, --date <date>  Which day of the run (default its first day with bars).
  -a, --all          Every candle, not just the ones where a condition changed, fired or traded. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof backtest conditions bt-1a2b3c4d
  idiotproof backtest conditions bt-1a2b3c4d --date 2026-10-29 --all
```

### backtest run

```text
Backtest a saved strategy or a script over a range of ET days with StrategyBacktester: triggers, trades and P&L per day (saved for backtest conditions).

Usage: idiotproof backtest run [<strategy>] [--script <string>] [--from <date>] [--to <date>] [--qty <int>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <strategy>             A saved strategy: id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol (or use --script).
      --script <string>  Backtest this IdiotScript, canonical JSON or stamp instead of a saved strategy (`-` reads stdin).
      --from <date>      First ET trading day (yyyy-MM-dd); default the last completed trading day.
      --to <date>        Last ET trading day (yyyy-MM-dd); default --from.
      --qty <int>        Share count when the strategy doesn't pin one (default 100). (default: 100)

Examples:
  idiotproof backtest run NVDA --from 2026-10-26 --to 2026-10-30
  idiotproof backtest run --script "Ticker(\"INTC\").IsAboveVwap().StopLoss(2).TakeProfit(4)" --from 2026-10-29
```

### crypto bars

```text
OHLCV bars for a crypto pair from Alpaca's US crypto feed (times in ET).

Usage: idiotproof crypto bars <pair> [--timeframe <string>] [--hours <int>] [--limit <int>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <pair>                    Crypto pair, e.g. BTC/USD. (required)
      --timeframe <string>  Bar size in Alpaca's form: 1Min, 5Min, 15Min, 1Hour, 4Hour, 1Day, 1Week (default 1Hour). (default: 1Hour)
      --hours <int>         How far back to look, in hours (default 24). (default: 24)
      --limit <int>         Show at most this many bars, the most recent (default 48). (default: 48)

Examples:
  idiotproof crypto bars BTC/USD
  idiotproof crypto bars ETH/USD --timeframe 5Min --hours 2
```

### crypto buy

```text
Buy a crypto pair (fractional, GTC/IOC) through the TransactionGateway. Paper by default; live needs a confirmation code.

Usage: idiotproof crypto buy <pair> [<qty>] [--notional <decimal>] [--limit <decimal>] [--trigger <decimal>] [--stop <decimal>] [--target <decimal>] [--tif <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--note <string>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <pair>                           Crypto pair, e.g. BTC/USD. (required)
  <qty>                            Coin quantity, fractional allowed (0.0015). Leave out and pass --notional to size by dollars.
      --notional <decimal>         Size by dollar amount instead of coin quantity.
  -l, --limit <decimal>            Limit price. Without it the order is a market order.
      --trigger <decimal>          Stop trigger price: with --limit it makes a stop-limit order.
  -s, --stop <decimal>             Protective stop price for a buy; the Risk Guardian refuses entries without one.
  -t, --target <decimal>           Take-profit price (for the reward:risk check).
      --tif <string>               Time in force: gtc (default) or ioc. (default: gtc)
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  paper (default) or live (needs a confirmation code). Sandbox does not simulate crypto. (default: paper)
      --note <string>              Why: kept in the audit trail.

Examples:
  idiotproof crypto buy BTC/USD 0.001 --limit 70000 --stop 66500
      Paper limit buy with a protective stop for the Risk Guardian.
  idiotproof crypto buy ETH/USD --notional 250 --stop 2300 --mode live
      Live dollar-sized buy; prints a confirmation code first.
```

```text
Sell crypto you hold (crypto is long-only). Exits always clear the gates; live needs a confirmation code.

Usage: idiotproof crypto sell <pair> [<qty>] [--notional <decimal>] [--limit <decimal>] [--trigger <decimal>] [--stop <decimal>] [--target <decimal>] [--tif <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--note <string>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <pair>                           Crypto pair, e.g. BTC/USD. (required)
  <qty>                            Coin quantity, fractional allowed (0.0015). Leave out and pass --notional to size by dollars.

  -l, --limit <decimal>            Limit price. Without it the order is a market order.
      --trigger <decimal>          Stop trigger price: with --limit it makes a stop-limit order.
  -s, --stop <decimal>             Protective stop price for a buy; the Risk Guardian refuses entries without one.
  -t, --target <decimal>           Take-profit price (for the reward:risk check).
      --tif <string>               Time in force: gtc (default) or ioc. (default: gtc)
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  paper (default) or live (needs a confirmation code). Sandbox does not simulate crypto. (default: paper)
      --note <string>              Why: kept in the audit trail.

Examples:
  idiotproof crypto sell BTC/USD 0.001
  idiotproof crypto sell ETH/USD --notional 100 --limit 2600 --tif ioc --mode live
```

## docs

### docs dsl

```text
Explain one IdiotScript verb: phase, signatures, meaning, doc comment, an example from its real signature, and uses.

Usage: idiotproof docs dsl <verb>
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <verb>  An IdiotScript verb or alias: StopLoss, IsAboveVwap, OnReclaim, RequireAdxAbove, ... (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof docs dsl StopLoss
  idiotproof docs dsl IsAboveVwap --json
```

### docs explain

```text
Explain a type or member: its doc comment, where it is declared (path:line), its members and its callers.

Callers are found by text (every line naming it as a whole word, comments and the declaration skipped), so overloads and same-named members elsewhere also show.

Usage: idiotproof docs explain <symbol> [--callers <int>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <symbol>             A type or member: TransactionGateway, TransactionGateway.SubmitAsync, a full name, or an XML doc id (T:..., M:...). (required)
      --callers <int>  Most lines that mention it to list (default 15; 0 for none). (default: 15)

Examples:
  idiotproof docs explain TransactionGateway
  idiotproof docs explain TransactionGateway.SubmitAsync --callers 5
  idiotproof docs explain T:IdiotProof.Core.Trading.OrderIntent --json
```

### docs law

```text
Show one BIBLE law (IP-LAW-n) in full, or list every law.

Usage: idiotproof docs law [<n>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <n>  The law: 3, LAW-3 or IP-LAW-3. Leave out to list every law.

Examples:
  idiotproof docs law 3
  idiotproof docs law
      Every law with its title and line.
```

### docs search

```text
Search everything IdiotProof knows about itself: BIBLE, docs, stories, tickets, code docs and catalogs.

Results are ranked: an exact id first, then entries holding every word (title and id hits weigh most). Follow up with `docs law`, `docs section`, `docs story`, `docs ticket` or `docs explain`.

Usage: idiotproof docs search <text>... [--kind <section|law|doc|story|ticket|symbol|catalog>] [--limit <int>] [--refresh]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <text>                                                    What to look for: words, a phrase, or an id like IP-LAW-3, IP-US-K1, IP-T259, §4, TransactionGateway. (required)
      --kind <section|law|doc|story|ticket|symbol|catalog>  Only one kind: section, law, doc, story, ticket, symbol or catalog.
      --limit <int>                                         Most results to show (default 15). (default: 15)
      --refresh                                             Re-read the docs, code and tickets first (the index otherwise refreshes every 30 minutes). (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof docs search transaction gateway
  idiotproof docs search "peak giveback" --kind story
  idiotproof docs search IP-LAW-9 --json
      Machine-readable hits with path:line and a snippet.
```

### docs section

```text
Show one BIBLE section (IP-§n, subsections included), or the table of contents.

Usage: idiotproof docs section [<section>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <section>  The BIBLE section: 4, §4, 4.4 or IP-§4. Leave out to list the sections.

Examples:
  idiotproof docs section 4
  idiotproof docs section 4.4
      A numbered subsection.
  idiotproof docs section
      The BIBLE's table of contents.
```

### docs story

```text
Show one user story (IP-US-*) with its status and proving tests, or list an epic's stories.

Usage: idiotproof docs story [<id>] [--epic <string>] [--status <string>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <id>                   The story: K1, US-K1 or IP-US-K1. Leave out and pass --epic or --status to list stories.
      --epic <string>    List the stories of one epic by letter (K, W, ...).
      --status <string>  List only stories with this status: done, partial or planned.

Examples:
  idiotproof docs story K1
  idiotproof docs story --epic W
      Every Epic W story with its status.
  idiotproof docs story --status planned
```

### docs ticket

```text
Show one ticket: status, description, requires / required-by, the commits that name it, and its history.

Usage: idiotproof docs ticket <id> [--history]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <id>           The ticket: IP-T259, T259 or 259. (required)
      --history  Also list every recorded change (status, priority, approval, links) with its ET time. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof docs ticket IP-T259
  idiotproof docs ticket 266 --history
```

### dsl format

```text
Usage: idiotproof dsl glossary [<verb>]
Risk: read

Parameters:

  idiotproof dsl glossary IsAboveVwap
```

### dsl parse

```text
Parse IdiotScript (or JSON or a stamp) into the canonical strategy JSON the Monitor evaluates; nothing is saved.

Usage: idiotproof dsl parse <text>
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <text>  IdiotScript, canonical JSON or a stamp; `-` reads it from stdin. (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof dsl parse "Ticker(\"NVDA\").IsAboveVwap().Long().StopLoss(2).TakeProfit(5)"
  idiotproof dsl parse -
      Reads the script from stdin, e.g. `type nvda.idiot | idiotproof dsl parse -`.
```

### dsl validate

```text
Validate IdiotScript/JSON against the phase rules and the gates, failing closed with every reason (nothing is saved).

Usage: idiotproof dsl validate <text>
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <text>  IdiotScript, canonical JSON or a stamp; `-` reads it from stdin. (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof dsl validate "Ticker(\"NVDA\").IsAboveVwap().Long().StopLoss(2).TakeProfit(5)"
  idiotproof dsl validate -
      Reads the script or JSON from stdin.
```

### dsl verbs

```text
The IdiotScript verb catalog by phase, reflected from the code that compiles it (IP-LAW-4).

Usage: idiotproof dsl verbs [--phase <string>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --phase <string>  Only one phase: setup, filters, entry, order, risk, exit, or conditions (the static If/ElseIf catalog).

Examples:
  idiotproof dsl verbs
  idiotproof dsl verbs --phase risk
  idiotproof dsl verbs --phase conditions
      The static Conditions catalog used inside .If/.ElseIf.
```

## gapper

### gapper apply-tuned

```text
Save a backtest's hindsight-tuned profile as a new gapper strategy (inactive unless --arm).

Usage: idiotproof gapper apply-tuned <run> [--arm] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <run>                            The run id `gapper backtest-day` printed (gb-xxxxxxxx). (required)
      --arm                        Arm it right away (one-per-symbol and the 3-gapper cap still apply). (default: false)
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Broker mode for the new gapper: paper (default) or sandbox. (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof gapper apply-tuned gb-1a2b3c4d
  idiotproof gapper apply-tuned gb-1a2b3c4d --arm
```

### gapper arm

```text
Arm a gapper: activate an existing one or queue a new one from a profile, honoring one-per-symbol and the 3-gapper cap.

Usage: idiotproof gapper arm <gapper> [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--profile <string>] [--gap <number>] [--max-gap <number>] [--volume <number>] [--min-price <number>] [--max-price <number>] [--entry-start <string>] [--entry-end <string>] [--stop <number>] [--trail <number>] [--giveback <number>] [--arm-exit <string>] [--sell-by <string>] [--notional <decimal>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <gapper>                         A symbol (queues a new gapper when it has none) or a gapper's id, id prefix or stamp id. (required)
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Broker mode for a newly queued gapper: paper (default) or sandbox. Live is `strategy mode`, confirmed. (default: paper)
  -p, --profile <string>           Gapper profile id or name to start from (default classic-gapper).
      --gap <number>               Minimum gap over the previous close, percent.
      --max-gap <number>           Gap ceiling in percent (0 = no ceiling).
      --volume <number>            Premarket volume must be at least this multiple of average volume.
      --min-price <number>         Lowest price that qualifies.
      --max-price <number>         Highest price that qualifies.
      --entry-start <string>       Entry window start, ET (HH:mm).
      --entry-end <string>         Entry window end, ET (HH:mm).
      --stop <number>              Hard stop below entry, percent.
      --trail <number>             Trailing stop off the high, percent (0 = none).
      --giveback <number>          Sell once price gives back this percent of the entry-to-peak run.
      --arm-exit <string>          ET time the giveback exit arms (HH:mm).
      --sell-by <string>           Hard flatten time, ET (HH:mm), before the 9:30 bell.
      --notional <decimal>         Position size in dollars.

Examples:
  idiotproof gapper arm NVDA
  idiotproof gapper arm ABCD --profile penny-runner --stop 6
  idiotproof gapper arm 0190a3f2
```

```text
Every ticker an auto-gapper scan screened on a day: signals, the adaptive plan it chose, and armed or why skipped.
```

```text
Replay a gapper profile over one past day: fills, MFE/MAE, the giveback grid and a hindsight-tuned profile (saved for apply-tuned).

Risk: read

Parameters:

      --gap <number>          Minimum gap over the previous close, percent.

      --stop <number>         Hard stop below entry, percent.

      --arm-exit <string>     ET time the giveback exit arms (HH:mm).
      --sell-by <string>      Hard flatten time, ET (HH:mm), before the 9:30 bell.
      --notional <decimal>    Position size in dollars.

Examples:
```

```text
Dial a gapper profile in for one ticker and show the strategy GapperScriptFactory generates; --save stores it inactive.

  <symbol>                         The ticker to build the gapper for. (required)
  -s, --save                       Save it as an inactive gapper strategy (arm it later with `gapper arm`). (default: false)
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Broker mode for a saved gapper: paper (default) or sandbox. (default: paper)
  -p, --profile <string>           Gapper profile id or name to start from (default classic-gapper).
      --gap <number>               Minimum gap over the previous close, percent.
      --max-gap <number>           Gap ceiling in percent (0 = no ceiling).
      --volume <number>            Premarket volume must be at least this multiple of average volume.
      --min-price <number>         Lowest price that qualifies.
      --max-price <number>         Highest price that qualifies.
      --entry-start <string>       Entry window start, ET (HH:mm).
      --entry-end <string>         Entry window end, ET (HH:mm).
      --stop <number>              Hard stop below entry, percent.
      --trail <number>             Trailing stop off the high, percent (0 = none).
      --giveback <number>          Sell once price gives back this percent of the entry-to-peak run.
      --arm-exit <string>          ET time the giveback exit arms (HH:mm).
      --sell-by <string>           Hard flatten time, ET (HH:mm), before the 9:30 bell.
      --notional <decimal>         Position size in dollars.

Examples:
  idiotproof gapper tune NVDA --profile classic-gapper
  idiotproof gapper tune ABCD --profile penny-runner --gap 12 --stop 6 --giveback 18 --sell-by 09:25 --save
```

## hub

### hub install-service

```text
Install the Hub as a Windows service that runs as you (Monitor off unless --monitor).

Runs sc.exe create/description/failure and sets the service's environment in the registry. Needs an elevated Hub; otherwise it prints the commands and points at tools\install-hub-service.ps1, which elevates itself. Grant the account 'Log on as a service' (the script does). Stop any interactive Hub first: both use port 5910.

Usage: idiotproof hub install-service [--exe <string>] [--account <string>] [--password <string>] [--monitor] [--start <string>] [--dry-run]
Risk: destructive

Parameters:
      --exe <string>       The Hub exe the service runs (default: the published C:\Apps\IdiotProof\Hub\idiotproof-hub.exe).
      --account <string>   Windows account to run as (default: you, as DOMAIN\user or .\user). Must be the user who owns the LocalDB database and keys.
      --password <string>  That account's Windows password (required unless --dry-run; never logged).
      --monitor            Host the trading Monitor in the service (it places real orders unattended). Off by default. (default: false)
      --start <string>     Start type: delayed-auto (default), auto or demand. (default: delayed-auto)
      --dry-run            Show the commands without running them. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof hub install-service --dry-run
  idiotproof hub install-service --password "..." --monitor
```

### hub ping

```text
Check the Hub is up and show its clock in ET.

Usage: idiotproof hub ping
Risk: read

Examples:
  idiotproof hub ping
```

### hub uninstall-service

```text
Stop and remove the Hub's Windows service.

sc.exe stop (graceful: the Hub drains operations, stops the Monitor and releases the leader lease), then sc.exe delete. Needs an elevated Hub; otherwise prints the commands. Run it from an interactive Hub or the script, not the service's own Hub.

Usage: idiotproof hub uninstall-service [--dry-run]
Risk: destructive

Parameters:
      --dry-run  Show the commands without running them. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof hub uninstall-service --dry-run
  idiotproof hub uninstall-service
```

## keys

### keys migrate-to-vault

```text
Move Alpaca keys, OAuth tokens and Claude keys out of SQL into MindAttic.Vault (dry run unless --apply).

Per user and secret: copy into Vault when Vault lacks it, verify equality when both have it, then clear the SQL column. Conflicts and undecryptable values are reported and left untouched. Idempotent.

Usage: idiotproof keys migrate-to-vault [--apply]
Risk: destructive

Parameters:
      --apply  Actually copy into Vault and clear the SQL columns (without it: a dry run that changes nothing). (default: false)

  idiotproof keys migrate-to-vault --apply
```

## monitor

### monitor heartbeat

```text
The Monitor loop's last heartbeat: when it ticked, ok or fail, failures in a row.

Reads the SupervisedLoop heartbeat file (Logs\monitor.heartbeat), which the loop rewrites after every tick, hosted here or not. Exit 3 (blocked) when it is stale.

Usage: idiotproof monitor heartbeat
Risk: read

Examples:
  idiotproof monitor heartbeat
```

### monitor lease

```text
Who holds the Monitor's SQL leader lease (only the holder evaluates and trades).

One Monitor per database trades: it holds sp_getapplock 'IdiotProof.Monitor.Leader'. Shows the holder's PID and machine when SQL Server reports them.

Usage: idiotproof monitor lease
Risk: read

Examples:
  idiotproof monitor lease
```

### monitor pause

```text
Pause the Monitor: from its next tick it evaluates nothing - no entries and NO exits - until resumed.

Sets the SettingsKv flag monitor.paused, honored at the top of every tick (within 2 s). The loop, heartbeat and leader lease stay up. Open positions are not managed while paused - flatten them first if that matters.

Usage: idiotproof monitor pause [--reason <string>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
      --reason <string>  Why (kept with the flag and shown by `monitor status`).

Examples:
  idiotproof monitor pause
  idiotproof monitor pause --reason "news pending"
```

### monitor resume

```text
Resume a paused Monitor (needs a confirmation code when a Live strategy is active).

Clears the SettingsKv flag monitor.paused; the Monitor evaluates again from its next tick. When any active strategy routes Live the first call returns a code: resuming means real-money entries.

Usage: idiotproof monitor resume
Risk: money

Examples:
  idiotproof monitor resume
  idiotproof monitor resume --confirm K7Q2M9
```

### monitor status

```text
Is the Monitor trading? Hosted, lease, last tick, paused, window, active strategies.

Reads the Hub's in-process Monitor state, the SettingsKv pause flag, the SQL leader lease and the heartbeat file. Times are ET.

Usage: idiotproof monitor status
Risk: read

Examples:
  idiotproof monitor status
  idiotproof monitor status --json
```

### monitor tail

```text
Recent Monitor activity: gate verdicts (fire, veto, block, entry, exit, reject) and live condition progress.

A snapshot of the last --minutes of the Monitor's audit trail (your strategies' events plus its start/stop/pause events), newest last, followed by where each of your active strategies stands. Run it again to follow.

Usage: idiotproof monitor tail [--lines <int>] [--minutes <int>] [--progress]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  -n, --lines <int>    Most recent events to show (1-500). (default: 40)
      --minutes <int>  How far back to look for events (1-1440). (default: 60)
      --progress       Also show each active strategy's live condition progress. (default: true)

Examples:
  idiotproof monitor tail
  idiotproof monitor tail --lines 100 --minutes 390
  idiotproof monitor tail --no-progress
```

### monitor tick-once

```text
Run one evaluation pass over your active strategies and show each verdict - never places, cancels or records an order.

Gate 1 only (entry conditions against fresh bars from the Hub's feed); the LLM panel, RiskGuardian and the broker are never called, and no position, progress row or live bar is written. Without --dry the pass is noted in the audit log.

Usage: idiotproof monitor tick-once [--dry] [--symbol <string>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --dry              Write nothing at all (by default the pass is recorded in the audit log as monitor-tick-once). (default: false)
      --symbol <string>  Only strategies on this symbol.

Examples:
  idiotproof monitor tick-once --dry
  idiotproof monitor tick-once --symbol NVDA
```

### options buy

```text
Buy option contracts to open (level 2+). Sandbox by default; live needs a confirmation code.

Usage: idiotproof options buy <occ> <contracts> [--limit <decimal>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--note <string>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <occ>                            OCC contract symbol, e.g. AAPL261219C00150000. (required)
  <contracts>                      Whole contracts (each is usually 100 shares). (required)
  -l, --limit <decimal>            Limit price per share (premium). Without it the order is a market order.
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Where it routes: sandbox (simulator, the default), paper, or live (needs confirmation). (default: sandbox)
      --note <string>              Why — kept in the audit trail.

Examples:
  idiotproof options buy AAPL261219C00150000 2 --limit 3.20 --mode paper
      Paper limit buy of 2 calls.
  idiotproof options buy SPY261120P00560000 1 --mode live
      Live market buy; prints a confirmation code first.
```

```text
An underlying's option chain for one expiration: calls and puts by strike with bid/ask, IV, delta and open interest.

Risk: read

      --strikes <int>           Strikes to show on each side of the spot price (default 10; 0 shows every strike). (default: 10)
```

```text

      --note <string>              Why — kept in the audit trail.
```

## orders

### orders bracket

```text
Entry plus a take-profit and a stop-loss that cancel each other (Alpaca bracket). The stop-loss is the Risk Guardian's stop.

Usage: idiotproof orders bracket <symbol> <side> <qty> [--limit <decimal>] [--take-profit <decimal>] [--stop-loss <decimal>] [--stop-loss-limit <decimal>] [--tif <string>] [--client-id <string>] [--stop <decimal>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--note <string>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <symbol>                         Ticker, e.g. NVDA. (required)
  <side>                           buy or sell (the parent's side; an OCO's side closes the position: sell exits a long). (required)
  <qty>                            Whole shares. (required)
  -l, --limit <decimal>            Entry limit price (bracket/OTO). Without it the entry is a market order.
      --take-profit <decimal>      Take-profit child's limit price.
      --stop-loss <decimal>        Stop-loss child's stop price.
      --stop-loss-limit <decimal>  Make the stop-loss a stop-limit with this limit price.
      --tif <string>               Time in force: day (default) or gtc. (default: day)
      --client-id <string>         Your own id for the parent order (Alpaca client_order_id).
  -s, --stop <decimal>             Planned protective stop for the Risk Guardian when the order has no stop-loss child (OTO with only a take-profit).
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Where it routes: sandbox (simulator, the default), paper, or live (needs confirmation). (default: sandbox)
      --note <string>              Why — kept in the audit trail.

Examples:
  idiotproof orders bracket NVDA buy 10 --limit 131 --take-profit 140 --stop-loss 127 --tif gtc --mode paper
  idiotproof orders bracket AAPL buy 5 --take-profit 240 --stop-loss 220 --stop-loss-limit 219.5
      Market entry; the stop-loss is a stop-limit.
```

```text
Examples:
```

```text
  <symbol>                                                 Ticker, e.g. NVDA. (required)
  <side>                                                   buy or sell. (required)
  <qty>                                                    Shares; fractions allowed (0.25, DAY only). Leave out and pass --notional to size by dollars.
      --notional <decimal>                                 Size by dollar amount instead of shares (DAY only).
      --type <market|limit|stop|stop-limit|trailing-stop>  market, limit, stop, stop-limit or trailing-stop. Default: worked out from the prices given (none = market).
  -l, --limit <decimal>                                    Limit price (limit and stop-limit orders).
      --stop-price <decimal>                               Stop trigger price (stop and stop-limit orders).
      --trail-percent <decimal>                            Trailing stop distance in percent.
      --trail-price <decimal>                              Trailing stop distance in dollars.
      --tif <string>                                       Time in force: day (default), gtc, opg (at the open), cls (at the close), ioc or fok. (default: day)
      --ext                                                Extended hours (premarket/after-hours); limit + day only. (default: false)
      --client-id <string>                                 Your own order id (Alpaca client_order_id, up to 128 characters).
      --intent <string>                                    Position intent: buy-to-open, buy-to-close, sell-to-open or sell-to-close.
  -s, --stop <decimal>                                     Planned protective stop for an entry (the Risk Guardian refuses entries without one).
  -t, --target <decimal>                                   Planned take-profit (for the reward:risk check).
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>                          Where it routes: sandbox (simulator, the default), paper, or live (needs confirmation). (default: sandbox)
      --note <string>                                      Why — kept in the audit trail.

Examples:
  idiotproof orders place NVDA buy 10 --limit 131.20 --stop 127.50 --tif gtc --mode paper
  idiotproof orders place AAPL buy 0.5 --stop 220 --mode paper
      Fractional market buy (DAY only).
  idiotproof orders place TSLA sell 5 --type trailing-stop --trail-percent 3 --tif gtc --mode paper
      Trailing stop exit.
  idiotproof orders place NVDA sell 10 --type stop-limit --stop-price 120 --limit 119.5 --client-id exit-nvda-1 --mode live
```

### orders replace

```text
Change a working order's quantity, limit/stop/trail, TIF or client id (Alpaca PATCH; it gets a new id). Through the gateway; live needs a code.

Usage: idiotproof orders replace <id> [--qty <decimal>] [--limit <decimal>] [--stop-price <decimal>] [--trail <decimal>] [--tif <string>] [--client-id <string>] [--stop <decimal>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--note <string>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <id>                             The working order to change (from `orders list`). (required)
      --qty <decimal>              New share count (fractions allowed).
  -l, --limit <decimal>            New limit price.
      --stop-price <decimal>       New stop trigger price.
      --trail <decimal>            New trailing distance, in the order's own unit (percent or dollars).
      --tif <string>               New time in force: day, gtc, opg, cls, ioc or fok.
      --client-id <string>         New client order id for the replacement order.
      --stop <decimal>             Protective stop for the position, needed when --qty raises an entry's size (the Risk Guardian checks the whole new size).
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  The account the order is in: paper (default) or live (needs confirmation). (default: paper)
      --note <string>              Why — kept in the audit trail.

Examples:
  idiotproof orders replace 61e69015-8549-4bfd-b9c3-01e75843f47d --limit 131.50
  idiotproof orders replace 61e69015-8549-4bfd-b9c3-01e75843f47d --qty 5 --tif gtc --mode live
```

### orders show

```text
One Alpaca order in full, by id or client id: prices, fills, timestamps (ET) and its nested bracket/OCO/OTO/multi-leg legs.

Usage: idiotproof orders show [<id>] [--client-id <string>] [--mode <all|paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <id>                         The Alpaca order id (from `orders list`). Leave out and pass --client-id to look up by your own id.
      --client-id <string>     Look the order up by its client order id instead.
      --mode <all|paper|live>  paper, live or all (default all: whichever account has it). (default: all)

Examples:
  idiotproof orders show 61e69015-8549-4bfd-b9c3-01e75843f47d
  idiotproof orders show --client-id exit-nvda-1 --mode paper
```

## positions

### positions close

```text
Close (or trim) one Alpaca position as a market exit through the TransactionGateway. Live needs a confirmation code.

Usage: idiotproof positions close <symbol> [--qty <decimal>] [--percentage <decimal>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--preview]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <symbol>                         Ticker or OCC option symbol of the position to close, e.g. NVDA. (required)
      --qty <decimal>              Close only this many shares/contracts (default: all of it).
      --percentage <decimal>       Close this percent of the position (0-100) instead of all of it.
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Which Alpaca account: paper (default) or live (needs a confirmation code). (default: paper)
      --preview                    Run every gate and show the exit without sending it. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof positions close HIHO --mode paper
  idiotproof positions close NVDA --percentage 50 --mode paper
      Sell half.
  idiotproof positions close TSLA --qty 5 --mode live
      Prints a confirmation code first.
```

### positions close-all

```text
Close every Alpaca position in one account with market exits through the TransactionGateway; optionally cancel open orders first. Live needs a confirmation code.

Usage: idiotproof positions close-all [--cancel-orders] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--preview]
Risk: money

Parameters:
      --cancel-orders              Cancel every open order first (frees shares held by working sells/stops). (default: false)
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Which Alpaca account: paper (default) or live (one confirmation code covers the whole set). (default: paper)
      --preview                    Run every gate and list everything that would close, without sending anything. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof positions close-all --preview
      List what would close in paper; send nothing.
  idiotproof positions close-all --cancel-orders --mode paper
  idiotproof positions close-all --cancel-orders --mode live
      Prints the full list and one confirmation code.
```

## replay

### replay all

```text

Risk: write

Parameters:

  <date>              The ET trading day (yyyy-MM-dd); default the last completed trading day.
      --pages         Render each run's page and the archive indexes (HTML only). (default: true)
      --out <string>  Archive folder for the pages (default the mindattic.com replays folder).

  idiotproof replay all NVDA 2026-10-29
```
