
### replay compare

```text
Two replay runs side by side: strategy, day, fires, round-trips, win rate, hold time and P&L, with the difference.

Usage: idiotproof replay compare <run-a> <run-b>
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <run-a>  First run id or prefix. (required)
  <run-b>  Second run id or prefix. (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof replay compare 0190a3f2 0190b7c1
```

### replay families

```text
The built-in strategy families `replay run --family` and `replay all` use, with what each trades.

Usage: idiotproof replay families
Risk: read

  idiotproof replay families
```

### replay list

```text
The replay archive, newest first: ticker, day, strategy, sim or live, fired and P&L.

Usage: idiotproof replay list [--symbol <string>] [--since <date>] [--kind <string>] [--fired] [--limit <int>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --symbol <string>  Only this ticker.
      --since <date>     Only runs of ET trading days on or after this date (yyyy-MM-dd).
      --kind <string>    Only sim (hypothetical replays) or live (the Monitor's real trades).
      --fired            Only runs that fired. (default: false)
      --limit <int>      At most this many runs, newest first (default 50). (default: 50)

Examples:

```

### replay live

```text
Render the Monitor's real trades for a day (from the trade diary) on that day's bars as LIVE runs in the archive.

Usage: idiotproof replay live [<symbol>] [--date <date>] [--pages] [--out <string>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <symbol>            Only this ticker (default every ticker the Monitor traded that day).
  -d, --date <date>   The ET day whose real trades to render (default today ET).
      --pages         Render the run pages and archive indexes (HTML only; publishing stays manual). (default: true)
      --out <string>  Archive folder for the pages (default the mindattic.com replays folder).

Examples:
  idiotproof replay live
  idiotproof replay live NVDA --date 2026-10-29
```

### replay regen

```text
Regenerate the replay archive's HTML (every run page and index) from SQL; never uploads or deploys.

Usage: idiotproof replay regen [--out <string>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
      --out <string>  Archive folder to (re)write (default the mindattic.com replays folder).

Examples:
  idiotproof replay regen
  idiotproof replay regen --out C:\temp\replays
```

### replay run

```text
Replay a strategy, gapper profile or built-in family over one past day with the Monitor's own evaluator; saves the run and its page.

Usage: idiotproof replay run <symbol> [<date>] [--strategy <string>] [--profile <string>] [--family <string>] [--repeat] [--pages] [--out <string>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <symbol>                 The ticker to replay. (required)
  <date>                   The ET trading day (yyyy-MM-dd); default the last completed trading day.
  -s, --strategy <string>  Replay this saved strategy (id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol) instead of the symbol's own.
  -p, --profile <string>   Replay a gapper profile on the fly (e.g. classic-gapper, penny-runner).
  -f, --family <string>    Replay a built-in family (momentum, reversal, rsireversal, emabreak, rthdrive, shortfade, swingreversal).
  -r, --repeat             Re-arm after every exit to show each round-trip the day offered. (default: false)
      --pages              Render the run page and archive indexes (HTML only; publishing stays manual). (default: true)
      --out <string>       Archive folder for the pages (default the mindattic.com replays folder).

Examples:
  idiotproof replay run NVDA 2026-10-29
  idiotproof replay run ABCD 2026-10-29 --profile penny-runner
  idiotproof replay run TSLA --family rthdrive --repeat --no-pages
```

```text

Risk: read

Parameters:
  <run>                Run id or its first 6+ characters (from `replay list`). (required)
      --bars <string>  Which per-bar rows to print: marked (entries/exits, default), session (in-session bars) or all. (default: marked)

```

## research

### research analyze

```text
Extract catalysts and portents from a ticker's news, a URL or pasted text via the LLM (--save to keep them).

Uses your Claude key (else the host's). Without --save nothing is written; with --save the claims join the research feed like scanned ones.

Usage: idiotproof research analyze <target> [--ticker <string>] [--text <string>] [--source <string>] [--days <int>] [--max-articles <int>] [--save]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <target>                  A ticker (analyzes its recent Alpaca news, or --text) or an http(s) URL of an article or filing. (required)
      --ticker <string>     The company a URL is about (required with a URL).
      --text <string>       Analyze this text instead of fetching anything.
      --source <string>     Source name to record (default: the URL's host, Alpaca's outlet, or "manual").
      --days <int>          News lookback for a ticker, 1-30 days (default 3). (default: 3)
      --max-articles <int>  Most news articles to analyze for a ticker, 1-20 (default 5). (default: 5)
      --save                Persist the extracted claims to the research feed (skips a URL already analyzed). (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof research analyze NVDA
  idiotproof research analyze https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/x.htm --ticker NVDA --save
  idiotproof research analyze AMD --text "AMD signs a preliminary $4B supply deal, closing next quarter"
```

```text
Parameters:
      --min-wait-days <int>  Only claims at least this many days old, 1-365 (default 5). (default: 5)
      --window-days <int>    Measure the price move this many days after the claim, 1-365 (default 7). (default: 7)
      --max <int>            Most claims to backfill this run, 1-5000 (default 200). (default: 200)
```

## scan

### scan movers

```text
Screen today's top gainers to the gapper band; --replay replays each survivor with a gapper profile and saves the runs.

Usage: idiotproof scan movers [--date <date>] [--replay] [--top <int>] [--min-gap <number>] [--min-price <number>] [--max-price <number>] [--profile <string>] [--pages] [--out <string>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  -d, --date <date>         ET day to replay the survivors on (default today ET — movers are live).
  -r, --replay              Replay each survivor with the gapper profile and save the runs (and pages). (default: false)
      --top <int>           Keep at most this many gappers (default 10, max 25). (default: 10)
      --min-gap <number>    Minimum percent change (default 5). (default: 5)
      --min-price <number>  Lowest price (default 1). (default: 1)
      --max-price <number>  Highest price (default 50). (default: 50)
  -p, --profile <string>    Gapper profile or family to replay with (default classic-gapper). (default: classic-gapper)
      --pages               With --replay: render run pages and archive indexes (HTML only). (default: true)
      --out <string>        Archive folder for the pages (default the mindattic.com replays folder).

Examples:
  idiotproof scan movers
  idiotproof scan movers --min-gap 10 --max-price 20 --replay
```

```text
Show one runtime setting: value, default, range and meaning.

```

### settings list

```text
List the app's runtime settings with current value, default, range and meaning.

Usage: idiotproof settings list [--all]

      --all  Also show internal bookkeeping keys the app writes for itself. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof settings list
  idiotproof settings list --all
```

```text
Change one runtime setting (type- and range-checked; unknown and internal keys refused).

Usage: idiotproof settings set <key> <value>
```

## strategy

### strategy activate

```text
Hand a strategy to the Monitor. A Live strategy needs a confirmation code.

Usage: idiotproof strategy activate <strategy>
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <strategy>  Id, id prefix, stamp id (IP-XXXX-XXXX) or symbol. (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy activate NVDA
```

### strategy bulk

```text
Activate or deactivate many strategies at once (--all, --symbol, --mode). Live activations need one confirmation code for the batch.

Deactivation skips strategies holding a position (that would orphan the exit). Activation skips quarantined and soft-deleted strategies; when the batch would turn on any Live strategy, nothing happens until you re-run with the confirmation code, which is bound to exactly that batch.

Usage: idiotproof strategy bulk <action> [--all] [--symbol <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <action>                         activate or deactivate. (required)
      --all                        Every strategy you own (soft-deleted ones excluded). (default: false)
      --symbol <string>            Only strategies on this symbol.
      --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Only strategies in this broker mode (sandbox, paper, live).

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy bulk deactivate --all
  idiotproof strategy bulk activate --symbol NVDA --mode paper
```

### strategy clone

```text
Copy a strategy (optionally onto another symbol) as a new, inactive Sandbox strategy.

The copy gets the same canon (re-validated), never the original's position, history or Live routing. Cloning onto another symbol warns about fixed prices that belonged to the original's chart.

Usage: idiotproof strategy clone <strategy> [--symbol <string>] [--title <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <strategy>                       Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol of the strategy to copy. (required)
      --symbol <string>            Trade a different symbol with the same rules.
      --title <string>             Title for the copy (default: "<title> (copy)").
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Broker mode for the copy: sandbox (default) or paper. (default: sandbox)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy clone NVDA
  idiotproof strategy clone NVDA --symbol AMD --title "AMD VWAP reclaim"
```

### strategy create

```text
Create a strategy from IdiotScript or canonical JSON after validating it. It starts inactive in Sandbox.

Exactly one of --script or --canon. A strategy with no size buys 1 share. Errors (no stop, stop on the wrong side of the target, a broken canon) stop the save; warnings are shown.

Usage: idiotproof strategy create [--script <string>] [--canon <string>] [--title <string>] [--ticker <string>] [--description <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--dry-run]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  -s, --script <string>            The strategy as IdiotScript text (`-` reads stdin).
      --canon <string>             The strategy as canonical JSON (what `strategy export --format json` prints) (`-` reads stdin).
      --title <string>             Title (default: the strategy's own name, else "SYM strategy").
      --ticker <string>            Symbol to use when the script doesn't name one.
      --description <string>       Free-form description stored with the strategy.
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Broker mode: sandbox (default) or paper. Live is a separate, confirmed step. (default: sandbox)
      --dry-run                    Validate and show the stamp without saving anything. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy create --script "Stock.Ticker(\"NVDA\").IsAboveVwap().Long().StopLoss(170).TakeProfit(190).Build()"
  idiotproof strategy create --canon - --mode paper
      Reads canonical JSON from stdin.
```

### strategy deactivate

```text
Stop the Monitor evaluating a strategy (refused while it holds a position).

Usage: idiotproof strategy deactivate <strategy>
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <strategy>  Id, id prefix, stamp id (IP-XXXX-XXXX) or symbol. (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy deactivate NVDA
```

### strategy delete

```text
Soft-delete a strategy: deactivate it and mark it [deleted] (reversible with --restore). Refused while it holds a position.

Deleting is a reversible disable (HOUSE-LAW-2): the row, canon and history stay, and `strategy list` hides it unless --deleted. --hard permanently removes a strategy that is already deleted — a separate, explicit second step.

Usage: idiotproof strategy delete <strategy> [--restore] [--hard]
Risk: destructive

Parameters:
  <strategy>     Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol. (required)
      --restore  Undo a delete: take the [deleted] marker off (it stays inactive). (default: false)
      --hard     Permanently remove an ALREADY deleted strategy and its progress row. Cannot be undone. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy delete NVDA
  idiotproof strategy delete 0193ab12 --restore
  idiotproof strategy delete 0193ab12 --hard
```

### strategy diff

```text
Compare two strategies field by field at the canon level (what the Monitor actually runs), plus title, mode and state.

Usage: idiotproof strategy diff <a> <b>
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <a>  First strategy: id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol. (required)
  <b>  Second strategy: id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol. (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy diff NVDA AMD
  idiotproof strategy diff IP-P4AY-UXZU IP-Q7RB-K2MD
```

### strategy explain

```text
Explain a strategy in plain English, phase by phase — generated from its canon, no LLM, the same words every time.

Usage: idiotproof strategy explain <strategy>
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <strategy>  Id, id prefix, stamp id (IP-XXXX-XXXX) or symbol. (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy explain NVDA
```

### strategy export

```text
Export a strategy as a stamp, armored payload, canonical JSON or IdiotScript.

Usage: idiotproof strategy export <strategy> [--format <stamp|armor|json|script>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <strategy>                              Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol. (required)
  -f, --format <stamp|armor|json|script>  stamp (default), armor (payload only), json (canonical) or script (IdiotScript). (default: stamp)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy export NVDA --format json
```

### strategy fires

```text
Why a strategy did or didn't fire: its recent gate verdicts (conditions met, LLM veto, Risk Guardian block, order placed or rejected) and where it stands now.

Usage: idiotproof strategy fires <strategy> [--limit <int>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <strategy>         Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol. (required)
  -n, --limit <int>  How many verdicts to show (default 20, max 200). (default: 20)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy fires NVDA
  idiotproof strategy fires NVDA --limit 50
```

### strategy from-text

```text
Turn a plain-English description into a strategy (via the LLM), show its stamp, and save it only when you confirm.

The first call writes the IdiotScript, validates it and shows the stamp with a confirmation code; nothing is saved. Re-run with --confirm <code> to save exactly what was shown (the LLM is not called again). It saves inactive, in Sandbox by default, 1 share when unsized.

Usage: idiotproof strategy from-text <description> [--ticker <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--title <string>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <description>                    The strategy in plain English (`-` reads stdin). (required)
  -t, --ticker <string>            The symbol to trade (default: the first ticker-looking word, e.g. $NVDA or NVDA).
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Broker mode for the saved strategy: sandbox (default) or paper. (default: sandbox)
      --title <string>             Title for the saved strategy (default: its own name, else "SYM strategy").

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy from-text "Buy NVDA when it reclaims VWAP with volume, stop 2% under, take profit at 190"
  idiotproof strategy from-text "long on a 9 EMA reclaim above VWAP, 3% stop" --ticker AMD --mode paper
```

### strategy from-watchlist

```text
Create one strategy per item of a watchlist JSON file (the Monitor's create-strategies, through the CLI).

Each item's script is validated like `strategy create`; an item that fails is reported and skipped. Items already present (same symbol and title) or repeated in the file are skipped, so re-running is safe. New strategies start inactive in Sandbox with 1 share when unsized; --activate turns on the items marked active.

Usage: idiotproof strategy from-watchlist <file> [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--activate] [--dry-run]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <file>                           A watchlist JSON file (absolute path: the Hub reads it), the JSON itself, or `-` for stdin: [{"title","symbol","script","description","author","originTranscript","active"}]. (required)
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Broker mode for every new strategy: sandbox (default) or paper. (default: sandbox)
      --activate                   Activate items marked "active": true (default: everything starts inactive). (default: false)
      --dry-run                    Validate every item and report what would happen without saving. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy from-watchlist D:/watchlists/2026-10-30.json
  idiotproof strategy from-watchlist -
      Reads the watchlist JSON from stdin, e.g. `type watchlist.json | idiotproof strategy from-watchlist -`.
  idiotproof strategy from-watchlist - --mode paper --activate --dry-run
```

### strategy history

```text
A strategy's trail, newest first: Monitor verdicts and fills, diary trades, and the CLI/MCP commands that touched it.

Usage: idiotproof strategy history <strategy> [--limit <int>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <strategy>         Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol. (required)
  -n, --limit <int>  How many events to show (default 40, max 500). (default: 40)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy history NVDA
  idiotproof strategy history NVDA --limit 100
```

### strategy import

```text
Create a strategy from a stamp, canonical JSON or IdiotScript. It starts inactive in Sandbox.

Usage: idiotproof strategy import <source> [--title <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <source>                         A pasted stamp/armor/IPS1 payload, canonical JSON, or IdiotScript text (`-` reads stdin). (required)
      --title <string>             Title for the new strategy (default: the strategy's own name or symbol).
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Broker mode for the new strategy: sandbox (default) or paper. Live is a separate, confirmed step. (default: sandbox)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy import -
      Reads the pasted stamp from stdin, e.g. `type gapper-stamp.txt | idiotproof strategy import -`.
  idiotproof strategy import "Ticker(\"NVDA\").IsAboveVwap().StopLoss(2)" --mode paper
```

### strategy list

```text
List your strategies with mode, position and live condition progress.

Usage: idiotproof strategy list [--active] [--symbol <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--deleted]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  -a, --active                     Only strategies the Monitor is evaluating. (default: false)
      --symbol <string>            Only this symbol.
      --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Only this broker mode (sandbox, paper, live).
      --deleted                    Include soft-deleted strategies (hidden by default). (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy list
  idiotproof strategy list --active --mode live
```

### strategy mode

```text
Route a strategy to sandbox, paper or live. Switching to live needs a confirmation code.

Usage: idiotproof strategy mode <strategy> <mode>
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <strategy>  Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol. (required)
  <mode>      sandbox, paper or live (live needs a confirmation code). (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy mode NVDA paper
  idiotproof strategy mode NVDA live
```

### strategy progress

```text
How close a strategy is to firing: conditions passing N/M, the first failing verb and the last price, optionally watched.

Reads the row the Monitor writes every tick. --watch samples it --samples times, --every seconds apart (at most two minutes in all), and reports each change; it stops early when every condition passes.

Usage: idiotproof strategy progress <strategy> [--watch] [--every <int>] [--samples <int>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <strategy>           Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol. (required)
  -w, --watch          Keep sampling the Monitor's progress row and report each change (bounded by --samples). (default: false)
      --every <int>    Seconds between samples while watching (0-60, default 5). (default: 5)
      --samples <int>  How many samples to take while watching (1-120, default 12). (default: 12)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy progress NVDA
  idiotproof strategy progress NVDA --watch --every 10 --samples 6
```

### strategy quarantine

```text
List strategies the Monitor refuses to evaluate (canon unreadable, or no canon and a script that doesn't parse), with the reason.

A quarantined strategy never fires; one that is quarantined while holding a position has NO managed exit and is listed first.

Usage: idiotproof strategy quarantine [--symbol <string>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --symbol <string>  Only this symbol.

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy quarantine
```

### strategy rename

```text
Give a strategy a new title. Its canon, stamp id and state are untouched.

Only the title changes, so the stamp id stays the same. The Monitor's audit lines carry the title at the time, so `strategy history` matches the new title from now on.

Usage: idiotproof strategy rename <strategy> <title>
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <strategy>  Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol. (required)
  <title>     The new title (1-200 characters). (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy rename NVDA "NVDA VWAP reclaim"
```

### strategy resync-canon

```text
Re-derive your strategies' canons from their scripts where the script now yields a richer canon; dry run unless --apply.

The repair for verbs an older parser dropped silently. A row is rewritten only when the re-derived canon has at least as many entry conditions and branches as the stored one; anything that would lose a condition is skipped and reported. Only the canon (ScriptJson) changes — position bookkeeping is untouched.

Usage: idiotproof strategy resync-canon [--apply]
Risk: write

Parameters:
      --apply  Write the repaired canons (default is a dry run that changes nothing). (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy resync-canon
  idiotproof strategy resync-canon --apply
```

### strategy samples

```text
List the built-in sample strategies, or show one as IdiotScript, a stamp or canonical JSON.

Samples are worked examples you can save and edit: `idiotproof strategy samples vwap-reclaim --format json | idiotproof strategy create --canon -`.

Usage: idiotproof strategy samples [<name>] [--format <stamp|armor|json|script>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <name>                                  A sample's name to show in full (omit to list them all).
  -f, --format <stamp|armor|json|script>  How to show one sample: script (default), stamp or json. (default: script)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy samples
  idiotproof strategy samples vwap-reclaim
  idiotproof strategy samples sune-wedge --format stamp
```

### strategy set

```text
Edit a strategy's stop, target, trailing, size, sell-by time or session; the canon is rewritten and re-validated.

Only the named fields change. The result must still validate (a stop, stop below target on a long, ...). A Live strategy needs a confirmation code bound to exactly these changes.

Usage: idiotproof strategy set <strategy> [--stop <decimal>] [--stop-percent <decimal>] [--target <decimal>] [--target-percent <decimal>] [--trailing <decimal>] [--giveback <decimal>] [--qty <int>] [--notional <decimal>] [--sell-by <string>] [--session <premarket|rth|after-hours|extended>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <strategy>                                          Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol. (required)
      --stop <decimal>                                Stop-loss price (replaces a percent stop).
      --stop-percent <decimal>                        Stop-loss percent from the fill (replaces a price stop).
      --target <decimal>                              Take-profit price (replaces a percent target and any scale-out ladder).
      --target-percent <decimal>                      Take-profit percent from the fill (replaces a price target).
      --trailing <decimal>                            Trailing-stop percent; 0 removes it.
      --giveback <decimal>                            Peak-giveback exit percent; 0 removes it.
      --qty <int>                                     Share quantity per entry (replaces a notional size).
      --notional <decimal>                            Dollar size per entry (replaces a share quantity).
      --sell-by <string>                              Sell anything still held at this ET time (HH:mm); "none" removes it.
      --session <premarket|rth|after-hours|extended>  Trading session: premarket, rth, afterhours or extended.

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy set NVDA --stop 168.5 --target 195
  idiotproof strategy set NVDA --qty 2 --sell-by 15:45
```

### strategy show

```text
Everything about one strategy: settings, script, position, progress.

Usage: idiotproof strategy show <strategy>
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <strategy>  Id, id prefix, stamp id (IP-XXXX-XXXX) or symbol. (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy show NVDA
  idiotproof strategy show IP-P4AY-UXZU
```

### strategy stamp

```text
Print the strategy's ASCII stamp: header, phase flow, exit ladder, fingerprint and a paste-back payload.

Usage: idiotproof strategy stamp <strategy> [--unicode] [--qr] [--compact]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <strategy>     Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol. (required)
  -u, --unicode  Box-drawing characters instead of plain ASCII. (default: false)
      --qr       Add a terminal QR code of the payload. (default: false)
      --compact  Leave out the armored payload block (picture only). (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy stamp NVDA
  idiotproof strategy stamp IP-P4AY-UXZU --unicode --qr
```

### strategy validate

```text
Check a saved strategy or a script: parse, canon round-trip, phase rules and a risk preview. Changes nothing.

Usage: idiotproof strategy validate [<strategy>] [--script <string>] [--canon <string>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <strategy>             Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol of a saved strategy (omit with --script/--canon).
  -s, --script <string>  Validate this IdiotScript text instead of a saved strategy (`-` reads stdin).
      --canon <string>   Validate this canonical JSON instead of a saved strategy (`-` reads stdin).

Examples:
  idiotproof strategy validate NVDA
  idiotproof strategy validate --script "Stock.Ticker(\"AMD\").IsAboveVwap().Long().StopLoss(150).Build()"
```

## trade

### trade buy

```text
Buy shares (open or add to a long). Sandbox by default; live needs a confirmation code.

Usage: idiotproof trade buy <symbol> [<qty>] [--dollars <decimal>] [--limit <decimal>] [--stop <decimal>] [--target <decimal>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--ext] [--tif <string>] [--note <string>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <symbol>                         Ticker, e.g. NVDA. (required)
  <qty>                            Shares. Leave out and pass --dollars to size by amount.
      --dollars <decimal>          Size by dollar amount instead of shares (fractional, regular hours only).
  -l, --limit <decimal>            Limit price. Without it the order is a market order.
  -s, --stop <decimal>             Protective stop price for an entry; the Risk Guardian refuses entries without one.
  -t, --target <decimal>           Take-profit price (for the reward:risk check).
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Where it routes: sandbox (simulator, the default), paper, or live (needs confirmation). (default: sandbox)
      --ext                        Extended hours (premarket/after-hours); requires --limit, DAY. (default: false)
      --tif <string>               Time in force: day (default) or gtc. (default: day)
      --note <string>              Why — kept in the audit trail.

Examples:
  idiotproof trade buy NVDA 10 --limit 131.20 --stop 127.50
      Sandbox limit buy with a protective stop.
  idiotproof trade buy AAPL --dollars 500 --stop 220 --mode paper
  idiotproof trade buy GAPT 100 --limit 4.12 --stop 3.90 --ext --mode live
      Premarket live buy; prints a confirmation code first.
```

### trade confirm

```text
Execute a pending Live order by its confirmation code (exactly what was previewed, once).

Usage: idiotproof trade confirm <code>
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <code>  The six-character code a Live preview returned. (required)

Examples:
  idiotproof trade confirm K7Q2ZP
```

### trade cover

```text
Buy to cover a short.

Usage: idiotproof trade cover <symbol> [<qty>] [--dollars <decimal>] [--limit <decimal>] [--stop <decimal>] [--target <decimal>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--ext] [--tif <string>] [--note <string>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <symbol>                         Ticker, e.g. NVDA. (required)
  <qty>                            Shares. Leave out and pass --dollars to size by amount.
      --dollars <decimal>          Size by dollar amount instead of shares (fractional, regular hours only).
  -l, --limit <decimal>            Limit price. Without it the order is a market order.
  -s, --stop <decimal>             Protective stop price for an entry; the Risk Guardian refuses entries without one.
  -t, --target <decimal>           Take-profit price (for the reward:risk check).
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Where it routes: sandbox (simulator, the default), paper, or live (needs confirmation). (default: sandbox)
      --ext                        Extended hours (premarket/after-hours); requires --limit, DAY. (default: false)
      --tif <string>               Time in force: day (default) or gtc. (default: day)
      --note <string>              Why — kept in the audit trail.

Examples:
  idiotproof trade cover TSLA 5 --mode paper
```

### trade flatten

```text
Flatten a symbol, a strategy's position, or the whole account with market exits through the TransactionGateway. Live needs a confirmation code.

Usage: idiotproof trade flatten [--symbol <string>] [--strategy <string>] [--all] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--preview]
Risk: money

Parameters:
      --symbol <string>            Close the whole broker position in this symbol.
      --strategy <string>          Close what this strategy books (id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol), capped at what the broker holds.
      --all                        Close every position in the account. (default: false)
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  paper or live (live needs a confirmation code). Default: the strategy's mode with --strategy, else paper.
      --preview                    Run every gate and list the exits without sending them. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof trade flatten --symbol HIHO --mode paper
  idiotproof trade flatten --strategy IP-P4AY-UXZU
      Uses the strategy's own mode.
  idiotproof trade flatten --all --mode live --preview
      List every Live exit without sending anything.
```

### trade notional

```text
Buy (or sell) a dollar amount of a stock: a fractional, DAY, market order sized in dollars. Live needs a code.

Usage: idiotproof trade notional <symbol> <amount> [--side <buy|sell>] [--stop <decimal>] [--target <decimal>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--note <string>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <symbol>                         Ticker, e.g. AAPL. (required)
  <amount>                         Dollars to buy (or sell) — Alpaca works out the fractional shares. (required)
      --side <buy|sell>            buy (default, opens/adds to a long) or sell (trims a long by dollar value). (default: buy)
  -s, --stop <decimal>             Protective stop price for a buy; the Risk Guardian refuses entries without one.
  -t, --target <decimal>           Take-profit price (for the reward:risk check).
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Where it routes: sandbox (simulator, the default), paper, or live (needs confirmation). (default: sandbox)
      --note <string>              Why — kept in the audit trail.

Examples:
  idiotproof trade notional AAPL 500 --stop 220 --mode paper
  idiotproof trade notional AAPL 250 --side sell --mode live
      Trim $250 of a long; prints a confirmation code first.
```

### trade sell

```text
Sell shares you hold (close or trim a long). Exits always clear the gates.

Usage: idiotproof trade sell <symbol> [<qty>] [--dollars <decimal>] [--limit <decimal>] [--stop <decimal>] [--target <decimal>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--ext] [--tif <string>] [--note <string>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <symbol>                         Ticker, e.g. NVDA. (required)
  <qty>                            Shares. Leave out and pass --dollars to size by amount.
      --dollars <decimal>          Size by dollar amount instead of shares (fractional, regular hours only).
  -l, --limit <decimal>            Limit price. Without it the order is a market order.
  -s, --stop <decimal>             Protective stop price for an entry; the Risk Guardian refuses entries without one.
  -t, --target <decimal>           Take-profit price (for the reward:risk check).
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Where it routes: sandbox (simulator, the default), paper, or live (needs confirmation). (default: sandbox)
      --ext                        Extended hours (premarket/after-hours); requires --limit, DAY. (default: false)

      --note <string>              Why — kept in the audit trail.
```

### trade short

```text
Sell short (open a short). Needs a stop above entry; margin + shortable name at the broker.

Usage: idiotproof trade short <symbol> [<qty>] [--dollars <decimal>] [--limit <decimal>] [--stop <decimal>] [--target <decimal>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--ext] [--tif <string>] [--note <string>]
Risk: money

Parameters:
  <symbol>                         Ticker, e.g. NVDA. (required)
  <qty>                            Shares. Leave out and pass --dollars to size by amount.
      --dollars <decimal>          Size by dollar amount instead of shares (fractional, regular hours only).
  -l, --limit <decimal>            Limit price. Without it the order is a market order.
  -s, --stop <decimal>             Protective stop price for an entry; the Risk Guardian refuses entries without one.
  -t, --target <decimal>           Take-profit price (for the reward:risk check).
  -m, --mode <sandbox|paper|live>  Where it routes: sandbox (simulator, the default), paper, or live (needs confirmation). (default: sandbox)
      --ext                        Extended hours (premarket/after-hours); requires --limit, DAY. (default: false)
      --tif <string>               Time in force: day (default) or gtc. (default: day)
      --note <string>              Why — kept in the audit trail.

Examples:
  idiotproof trade short TSLA 5 --limit 240 --stop 246
```

## users

### users create

```text
Create an IdiotProof account (blocklist and password rules of web sign-up; Argon2id via MindAttic.Authentication).

Usage: idiotproof users create <email> --password <string> [--role <string>] [--must-change]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <email>                  The new account's email (also its user name). (required)
      --password <string>  Initial password: 8 to 128 characters with at least one digit. (required)
      --role <string>      User (default) or Admin. (default: User)
      --must-change        Make them choose a new password at first sign-in. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof users create trader@example.com --password <password>
  idiotproof users create admin@example.com --password <password> --role Admin --must-change
```

### users list

```text
List the IdiotProof accounts (test fixtures hidden unless --all); * marks who you act as.

Usage: idiotproof users list [--all]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --all  Include test-fixture accounts (@idiotproof.local and bare user names), hidden by default. (default: false)

Examples:
  idiotproof users list
  idiotproof users list --all
```

## watchlist

### watchlist add

```text
Add symbols to your IdiotProof watchlist (creates a 'Main' workspace when you have none).

Usage: idiotproof watchlist add <symbols>... [--workspace <string>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <symbols>                 One or more ticker symbols (space or comma separated). (required)
      --workspace <string>  Which workspace (name or id); needed only when you have more than one.

Examples:
  idiotproof watchlist add NVDA AAPL
  idiotproof watchlist add TSLA --workspace Main
```

### watchlist list

```text
Your IdiotProof watchlist: the symbols on each of your workspaces (not Alpaca's watchlists).

Usage: idiotproof watchlist list [--workspace <string>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --workspace <string>  Only this workspace (name or id).

Examples:
  idiotproof watchlist list
  idiotproof watchlist list --workspace Main
```

### watchlist remove

```text
Remove symbols from your IdiotProof watchlist.

Usage: idiotproof watchlist remove <symbols>... [--workspace <string>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <symbols>                 One or more ticker symbols (space or comma separated). (required)
      --workspace <string>  Which workspace (name or id); needed only when you have more than one.

Examples:
  idiotproof watchlist remove AAPL
```

## watchlists

### watchlists add

```text
Add symbols to an Alpaca watchlist (by id or name).

Usage: idiotproof watchlists add <watchlist> <symbols>... [--mode <paper|live>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <watchlist>              Watchlist id or name. (required)
  <symbols>                One or more symbols (space or comma separated). (required)
      --mode <paper|live>  Alpaca account: paper (default) or live. (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof watchlists add tech AMD AVGO
```

### watchlists create

```text
Create an Alpaca watchlist, optionally with symbols.

Usage: idiotproof watchlists create <name> [<symbols>...] [--mode <paper|live>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <name>                   Name for the new watchlist. (required)
  <symbols>                Symbols to start with (space or comma separated).
      --mode <paper|live>  Alpaca account: paper (default) or live. (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof watchlists create tech AAPL MSFT NVDA
```

### watchlists delete

```text
Delete an Alpaca watchlist (by id or name).

Usage: idiotproof watchlists delete <watchlist> [--mode <paper|live>]
Risk: destructive

Parameters:
  <watchlist>              Watchlist id or name. (required)
      --mode <paper|live>  Alpaca account: paper (default) or live. (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof watchlists delete tech
```

### watchlists list

```text
Your Alpaca server-side watchlists (not IdiotProof's local watchlist): name, id, last update.

Usage: idiotproof watchlists list [--mode <paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
      --mode <paper|live>  Alpaca account: paper (default) or live. (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof watchlists list
  idiotproof watchlists list --mode live
```

### watchlists remove

```text
Remove symbols from an Alpaca watchlist (by id or name).

Usage: idiotproof watchlists remove <watchlist> <symbols>... [--mode <paper|live>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <watchlist>              Watchlist id or name. (required)
  <symbols>                One or more symbols (space or comma separated). (required)
      --mode <paper|live>  Alpaca account: paper (default) or live. (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof watchlists remove tech AMD
```

### watchlists rename

```text
Rename an Alpaca watchlist, keeping its symbols.

Usage: idiotproof watchlists rename <watchlist> <new-name> [--mode <paper|live>]
Risk: write

Parameters:
  <watchlist>              Watchlist id or current name. (required)
  <new-name>               The new name. (required)
      --mode <paper|live>  Alpaca account: paper (default) or live. (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof watchlists rename tech megacaps
```

### watchlists show

```text
One Alpaca watchlist (by id or name) and its symbols.

Usage: idiotproof watchlists show <watchlist> [--mode <paper|live>]
Risk: read

Parameters:
  <watchlist>              Watchlist id or name. (required)
      --mode <paper|live>  Alpaca account: paper (default) or live. (default: paper)

Examples:
  idiotproof watchlists show tech
  idiotproof watchlists show 3174d6df-7726-44b4-a5bd-7fda5ae6e009 --mode live
```
